meta.description: Comprehensive CEFR-leveled (A1-C2) English grammar content bank for a TOEFL preparation app, focused on the Structure/Grammar component. Content is designed for Turkish-native learners, with contrastive explanations, common-mistake distractor pairs, and TOEFL-style multiple-choice practice items per topic.
meta.description_tr: Bir TOEFL hazırlık uygulamasının Yapı/Dilbilgisi bölümü için tasarlanmış, CEFR seviyelerine (A1-C2) göre kategorize edilmiş kapsamlı İngilizce dilbilgisi içerik bankası. İçerik, Türkçe ana dilli öğrenciler için karşılaştırmalı açıklamalar, yaygın hata (distractor) çiftleri ve konu başına TOEFL formatında çoktan seçmeli alıştırma soruları içerecek şekilde tasarlanmıştır.
meta.target_audience: Turkish-native TOEFL candidates studying English grammar (Structure section) from beginner (A1) to advanced (C2) level.

'toefl_style_questions' are pre-built practice items with answer keys. Use 'difficulty_weight' to sequence topics within a level from easiest to hardest.

'toefl_style_questions' hazır cevap anahtarlı pratik sorulardır. 'difficulty_weight' alanı, bir seviye içindeki konuları kolaydan zora sıralamak için kullanılabilir.

topics.title: Verb 'To Be' (am/is/are)
topics.explanation: The verb 'to be' links a subject to a noun, adjective, or place, and is the single most fundamental verb in English. It has three present-tense forms depending on the subject: am (only with I), is (with he/she/it and singular nouns), are (with you/we/they and plural nouns). Unlike most English verbs, 'to be' does not need 'do/does' to form negatives or questions — the verb itself moves or takes 'not'. It is also used as an auxiliary in continuous tenses and passive voice, which students will meet later, so mastering its base forms early is essential.
topics.explanation_tr: 'To be' fiili özneyi bir isim, sıfat veya yer bildiren ifadeye bağlar ve İngilizce'deki en temel fiildir. Özneye göre üç şimdiki zaman biçimi vardır: am (sadece I ile), is (he/she/it ve tekil isimlerle), are (you/we/they ve çoğul isimlerle). Çoğu İngilizce fiilin aksine, 'to be' olumsuz ya da soru yaparken 'do/does' yardımcı fiiline ihtiyaç duymaz; fiilin kendisi yer değiştirir veya 'not' alır. Ayrıca continuous zamanlarda ve passive voice'ta yardımcı fiil olarak da kullanılır, bu yüzden temel biçimlerini erkenden sağlam öğrenmek çok önemlidir.
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Bu kelimeler genellikle 'to be' ile kurulan basit tanımlama veya durum cümlelerinde geçer; 'do/does' ile karıştırılmamalıdır.

exceptions.rule: Contractions (I'm, you're, he's) are used constantly in spoken and informal written English.
exceptions.example: I'm tired. / She's at home.
exceptions.explanation_tr: Konuşma dilinde ve gündelik yazıda 'to be' neredeyse her zaman kısaltılmış biçimde kullanılır; TOEFL yazılı bölümünde ise formal/resmî kayıtta genellikle açık biçim tercih edilir.

exceptions.rule: 'There is / There are' uses 'to be' but the real subject comes after the verb.
exceptions.example: There is a book on the table. (subject = 'a book', not 'there')
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'There' bir özne değil, cümleye giriş yapan bir öğedir; fiil gerçek öznenin (a book) sayısına göre uyumlanır.

examples.sentence: She is a doctor.
They are not ready yet.
Is he your brother?
We are students at this university.
I am not from Turkey; I am from Greece.

common_mistakes.wrong: She student.
common_mistakes.correct: She is a student.
common_mistakes.explanation: Turkish 'to be' can be a suffix (öğrenci-dir), so learners often drop the separate verb 'is' entirely in English.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Türkçe'de 'to be' çoğu zaman ek olarak eklenir (öğrencidir); bu yüzden Türk öğrenciler İngilizce'de ayrı bir fiil kullanmayı unutabilir.

common_mistakes.wrong: I am agree with you.
common_mistakes.correct: I agree with you.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Agree' is already a full verb in English; it does not need 'am/is/are' before it, unlike the Turkish pattern that implies a state.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Agree' İngilizce'de zaten tam bir fiildir; önüne 'am/is/are' eklenmez. Türkçe'de bir durum bildirir gibi hissedildiği için bu hata yaygındır.

common_mistakes.wrong: He don't is happy.
common_mistakes.correct: He isn't happy. / He is not happy.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'To be' never combines with 'do/does/don't' for negatives; 'not' attaches directly to am/is/are.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'To be' fiili olumsuz yaparken asla 'do/does/don't' ile birlikte kullanılmaz; 'not' doğrudan am/is/are'e eklenir.

common_mistakes.wrong: They is my friends.
common_mistakes.correct: They are my friends.
common_mistakes.explanation: The form of 'to be' must agree with the subject; 'they' always takes 'are', never 'is'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'To be' fiili özne ile uyumlu olmalıdır; 'they' her zaman 'are' alır, asla 'is' almaz.

common_mistakes.wrong: Where is you from?
common_mistakes.correct: Where are you from?
common_mistakes.explanation: Subject-verb agreement must hold in questions too; 'you' requires 'are', not 'is'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Sorularda da özne-fiil uyumu geçerlidir; 'you' 'are' gerektirir, 'is' değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: My parents ____ both teachers at the same school.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Özne 'my parents' çoğuldur, bu yüzden 'are' kullanılır.

toefl_style_questions.question: ____ she your cousin, or is she your neighbor?
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Tekil özne 'she' ile soru kurulurken yardımcı fiil olarak 'is' kullanılır, 'do/does' kullanılmaz.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL Structure questions test subject-verb agreement with 'to be' by hiding a plural/singular mismatch in a longer sentence, or by testing whether a form other than 'to be' (like 'do') has wrongly been inserted.

topics.title: Present Simple
topics.explanation: The present simple describes habits, routines, permanent facts, and general truths — actions that are not tied to a specific moment happening right now. For he/she/it, the verb takes an -s or -es ending; other subjects use the base form. Negatives and questions require the auxiliary 'do' (or 'does' for he/she/it), which then carries the -s ending instead of the main verb.
topics.explanation_tr: Present simple; alışkanlıkları, rutinleri, kalıcı gerçekleri ve genel doğruları anlatır — şu anda gerçekleşen belirli bir eylemi değil. He/she/it öznesiyle fiil -s veya -es alır; diğer öznelerde fiil yalın haliyle kullanılır. Olumsuz ve soru cümlelerinde 'do' (he/she/it için 'does') yardımcı fiili gerekir ve -s eki artık ana fiilden değil bu yardımcı fiilden alınır.
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Bu zarflar bir eylemin ne sıklıkla tekrarlandığını gösterir ve present simple kullanımının en güçlü işaretleridir.

exceptions.rule: Verbs ending in -ch, -sh, -ss, -x, -o take -es instead of just -s.
exceptions.example: watch → watches, go → goes, do → does
exceptions.explanation_tr: -ch, -sh, -ss, -x, -o ile bitn fiiller he/she/it ile -es alır, sadece -s değil.

exceptions.rule: Verbs ending in a consonant + y change y to i before adding -es.
exceptions.example: study → studies, fly → flies
exceptions.explanation_tr: Sessiz harf + y ile biten fiillerde y, i'ye dönüşür ve -es eklenir.

exceptions.rule: Stative verbs (know, believe, want, love, need, own) are almost never used in continuous form even when talking about 'now', so present simple covers this meaning too.
exceptions.example: I know the answer. (NOT: I am knowing the answer.)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Durum fiilleri (know, believe, want, love, need, own) continuous formda neredeyse hiç kullanılmaz; 'şu an' anlamını bile present simple ile verirler.

examples.sentence: The sun rises in the east.
She works at a hospital.
We don't eat meat on Fridays.
Does he speak French?
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

common_mistakes.wrong: She work every day.
common_mistakes.correct: She works every day.
common_mistakes.explanation: The -s ending for he/she/it is frequently forgotten because Turkish verb conjugation does not mark third-person singular the same way visually.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: He/she/it için gereken -s eki genellikle unutulur; çünkü Türkçe'de üçüncü tekil şahıs bu şekilde görsel olarak işaretlenmez.

common_mistakes.wrong: He doesn't likes coffee.
common_mistakes.correct: He doesn't like coffee.
common_mistakes.explanation: Once 'does' carries the -s, the main verb must return to its base form; adding -s twice is a very common Turkish-learner error.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Does' -s ekini üstlendiğinde ana fiil yalın haline döner; -s'i iki kere eklemek Türk öğrencilerde çok yaygın bir hatadır.

common_mistakes.wrong: Do she like tea?
common_mistakes.correct: Does she like tea?
common_mistakes.explanation: The auxiliary must also agree with the subject; 'she' requires 'does', not 'do'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Yardımcı fiil de özneyle uyumlu olmalıdır; 'she' 'does' gerektirir, 'do' değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: I am living in Istanbul since I was born.
common_mistakes.correct: I have lived in Istanbul since I was born.
common_mistakes.explanation: For a permanent situation continuing from the past to now, present perfect is needed, not present simple/continuous — a common overlap confusion.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Geçmişten bugüne süregelen kalıcı bir durum için present perfect gerekir, present simple/continuous değil — sık karıştırılan bir alandır.

common_mistakes.wrong: He always is late.
common_mistakes.correct: He is always late.
common_mistakes.explanation: Frequency adverbs go before the main verb but after 'to be'; word order with 'to be' is often transferred incorrectly from other verb patterns.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Sıklık zarfları ana fiilden önce, ama 'to be'den sonra gelir; bu sıralama diğer fiil kalıplarından yanlış aktarılabilir.

toefl_style_questions.question: Most birds ____ south before winter begins.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Özne 'most birds' çoğuldur, bu yüzden fiil yalın haliyle (-s'siz) kullanılır.

toefl_style_questions.question: The company rarely ____ its prices during the holiday season.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Özne tekil ('the company') olduğu için fiil -s alır: raises.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL commonly hides a missing or extra third-person -s in an otherwise correct sentence, or tests whether a stative verb has been wrongly put into a continuous form.

topics.title: Indefinite Articles (a/an)
topics.explanation: 'A' and 'an' introduce a singular, non-specific, countable noun for the first time. The choice between them depends on the sound (not the letter) that begins the next word: 'a' before a consonant sound, 'an' before a vowel sound. Articles are one of the hardest areas for Turkish learners because Turkish has no direct grammatical equivalent to 'a/an' or 'the'.
topics.explanation_tr: 'A' ve 'an', tekil, belirsiz, sayılabilir bir ismi ilk kez tanıtırken kullanılır. Aralarındaki seçim, sonraki kelimenin harfine değil sesine bağlıdır: sessiz harf sesinden önce 'a', sesli harf sesinden önce 'an' kullanılır. Artikeller Türk öğrenciler için en zor alanlardan biridir çünkü Türkçe'de 'a/an' veya 'the'ye doğrudan karşılık gelen bir yapı yoktur.
structure_patterns: a/an + (only with consonant/vowel SOUND, not letter)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Artikel seçimi kelimenin yazılışına değil söylenişine bakar; bu yüzden 'a university' ama 'an hour' gibi örnekler öğrencileri şaşırtır.

exceptions.rule: Words starting with a silent 'h' take 'an', even though 'h' is a consonant letter.
exceptions.example: an hour, an honest man
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'H' harfi sessiz okunduğunda (hour, honest) 'an' kullanılır, çünkü ses sesli harfle başlar.

exceptions.rule: Words starting with 'u' or 'o' that make a consonant sound (like 'yu' or 'wa') take 'a', not 'an'.
exceptions.example: a university, a one-way street
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'University' 'yu-' sesiyle başladığı için 'a' alır; 'one' 'wa-' sesiyle başladığı için de 'a' alır, harflerine bakılmaz.

exceptions.rule: Plural and uncountable nouns never take a/an.
exceptions.example: I need advice. (NOT: I need an advice.)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Çoğul ve sayılamayan isimlerle a/an asla kullanılmaz.

examples.sentence: I saw a cat in the garden.
She is an engineer.
He bought a used car.
examples.translation: O ikinci el bir araba aldı.

examples.sentence: It takes about an hour to get there.
examples.translation: Oraya gitmek yaklaşık bir saat sürüyor.

examples.sentence: This is a European city with a long history.
examples.translation: Bu, uzun bir geçmişe sahip Avrupalı bir şehir.

common_mistakes.wrong: She is a good student. She wants become a teacher.
common_mistakes.correct: She is a good student. She wants to become a teacher.
common_mistakes.explanation: This mixes an article issue with a missing infinitive marker; a common layered error, but here focus: articles are still needed before singular countable nouns like 'teacher'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Örnekte hem infinitive 'to' unutulmuş hem de artikel kullanımı gösterilmiştir; tekil sayılabilir isimlerden önce ('teacher') artikel gereklidir.

common_mistakes.wrong: I want to be doctor.
common_mistakes.correct: I want to be a doctor.
common_mistakes.explanation: Turkish does not require an article before a profession noun ('doktor olmak istiyorum'), so learners frequently omit 'a/an' entirely in English.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Türkçe'de meslek isminden önce artikel gerekmez ('doktor olmak istiyorum'); bu yüzden öğrenciler İngilizce'de 'a/an'i tamamen atlarlar.

common_mistakes.wrong: He is an university student.
common_mistakes.correct: He is a university student.
common_mistakes.explanation: Learners often choose the article based on the spelling ('u' looks like a vowel) rather than the actual pronunciation ('yu-' sound), which needs 'a'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Öğrenciler artikeli genellikle yazılışa göre seçer ('u' sesli harf gibi görünür), ama gerçek telaffuz ('yu-' sesi) 'a' gerektirir.

common_mistakes.wrong: I need an advices about this.
common_mistakes.correct: I need some advice about this.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable in English (unlike Turkish 'öneriler'), so it never takes 'a/an' or a plural -s.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Advice' İngilizce'de sayılamayan bir isimdir (Türkçe'deki 'öneriler'in aksine), bu yüzden asla 'a/an' veya çoğul -s almaz.

common_mistakes.wrong: She works as teacher at that school.
common_mistakes.correct: She works as a teacher at that school.
common_mistakes.explanation: After 'as' when identifying a role/profession, the article is still required, which is often skipped by Turkish speakers.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'As' ile bir rol/meslek belirtilirken artikel yine gereklidir; Türk öğrenciler bunu genelde atlar.

toefl_style_questions.question: It was ____ honor to meet such ____ influential scientist.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Honor' sessiz 'h' ile başladığı için 'an', 'influential' de sesli harf sesiyle başladığı için 'an' alır.

toefl_style_questions.question: My brother wants to become ____ architect after he finishes ____ two-year program.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Architect' sesli harf sesiyle başlar → 'an'; 'two-year' /tu/ sesiyle (sessiz gibi) başlar → 'a'.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL frequently tests article choice with tricky sound-vs-spelling cases (an hour, a university, a one-time offer) and with countable vs. uncountable nouns that differ between English and other languages.

topics.title: Plural Nouns
topics.explanation: Most English nouns form their plural by adding -s, but spelling changes apply depending on the noun's ending, and a set of common nouns have irregular plural forms that must be memorized individually rather than derived from a rule.
topics.explanation_tr: Çoğu İngilizce isim çoğul halini -s ekleyerek alır, ancak ismin sonuna göre yazım değişiklikleri uygulanır ve bazı yaygın isimlerin kurala bağlı olmayan, ezberlenmesi gereken düzensiz çoğul biçimleri vardır.
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Bu belirteçlerden sonra genellikle çoğul isim kullanılır; tekil isim kullanılması yaygın bir hatadır.

exceptions.rule: Nouns ending in a vowel + y just add -s (no change to y).
exceptions.example: boy → boys, day → days
exceptions.explanation_tr: Sesli harf + y ile biten isimlerde y değişmez, sadece -s eklenir.

exceptions.rule: Some nouns are irregular and must be memorized: man→men, woman→women, child→children, person→people, foot→feet, tooth→teeth, mouse→mice.
exceptions.example: Two children are playing outside.
exceptions.explanation_tr: Bu isimlerin çoğul halleri kurala uymaz, tek tek ezberlenmelidir.

exceptions.rule: Some nouns have the same singular and plural form.
exceptions.example: one fish / two fish, one sheep / two sheep
exceptions.explanation_tr: Bazı isimlerde tekil ve çoğul biçim aynıdır.

examples.sentence: There are three books on the shelf.
The buses were late this morning.
Many countries share this problem.
The children were playing in the park.
She has two brothers and one sister.
examples.translation: Onun iki erkek kardeşi ve bir kız kardeşi var.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have two informations for you.
common_mistakes.correct: I have two pieces of information for you.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable in English and has no plural form, even though its Turkish equivalent 'bilgiler' is naturally plural.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Information' İngilizce'de sayılamaz bir isimdir ve çoğul hali yoktur; Türkçe karşılığı 'bilgiler' doğal olarak çoğul olduğu için bu hata sık yapılır.

common_mistakes.wrong: There are many mans in the room.
common_mistakes.correct: There are many men in the room.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Man' has the irregular plural 'men'; adding a regular -s is a very frequent overgeneralization error.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Man' düzensiz çoğul 'men' alır; kurala göre -s eklemek çok yaygın bir aşırı genelleme hatasıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: Five year ago, I lived in Ankara.
common_mistakes.correct: Five years ago, I lived in Ankara.
common_mistakes.explanation: After a number greater than one, the noun must be plural; the -s is often dropped, especially in time expressions.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Birden büyük bir sayıdan sonra isim çoğul olmalıdır; özellikle zaman ifadelerinde -s eki çoğu zaman düşürülür.

common_mistakes.wrong: My family are big.
common_mistakes.correct: My family is big. / My family members are many.
common_mistakes.explanation: Collective nouns like 'family' are usually treated as singular in standard English (especially American English) when referring to the group as a unit.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Family' gibi kolektif isimler, özellikle Amerikan İngilizcesinde, grup tek bir birim olarak düşünüldüğünde tekil kabul edilir.

common_mistakes.wrong: The polices are investigating the case.
common_mistakes.correct: The police are investigating the case.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Police' is always plural in form and meaning and never takes -s or a singular verb.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Police' her zaman biçim ve anlam olarak çoğuldur; asla -s almaz ya da tekil fiil ile kullanılmaz.

toefl_style_questions.question: The research team collected ____ over a period of six months.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Data' genellikle sayılamayan bir isim gibi kullanılır ve çoğul -s almaz.

toefl_style_questions.question: Several ____ were injured in the accident, but no one was killed.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Person' kelimesinin düzensiz çoğulu 'people'dır; 'persons' çok resmi/hukuki bağlamlar dışında tercih edilmez ve 'peoples' farklı bir anlam taşır (halklar).

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL often tests irregular plurals (children, people, men) and uncountable nouns that are commonly pluralized incorrectly by non-native speakers (information, advice, data debates, equipment).

topics.title: Prepositions of Place
topics.explanation: Prepositions of place (in, on, at, under, between, behind, etc.) describe the physical location or spatial relationship of one thing to another. English prepositions rarely map one-to-one onto Turkish postpositions/case endings, so learners must memorize the specific preposition each expression requires rather than translating literally.
topics.explanation_tr: Yer edatları (in, on, at, under, between, behind vb.) bir şeyin fiziksel konumunu veya başka bir şeye göre uzamsal ilişkisini anlatır. İngilizce edatlar Türkçe'deki hâl eklerine/son eklere birebir karşılık gelmez; bu yüzden öğrenciler kelime kelime çeviri yapmak yerine her ifadenin gerektirdiği edatı ayrı ayrı ezberlemelidir.
structure_patterns: in + enclosed space/large area (in the box, in London)
on + surface (on the table, on the wall)
at + specific point (at the door, at the corner)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Bu edatlar genellikle konum sorularında ('where') ve TOEFL'da cümle içine yanlış edat yerleştirilerek test edilir.

exceptions.rule: 'At' is used for addresses and specific points, but 'in' is used for cities/countries and 'on' for streets.
exceptions.example: at 24 Main Street, on Main Street, in Paris
exceptions.explanation_tr: Aynı 'yer' fikri için bağlama göre farklı edatlar kullanılır: nokta için 'at', cadde için 'on', şehir/ülke için 'in'.

exceptions.rule: 'In' is used for vehicles you sit inside (car, taxi), but 'on' is used for vehicles you can walk around in (bus, train, plane, ship).
exceptions.example: in the car, on the bus
exceptions.explanation_tr: İçine oturduğunuz araçlarla (araba, taksi) 'in', içinde dolaşabildiğiniz araçlarla (otobüs, tren, uçak, gemi) 'on' kullanılır.

examples.sentence: The keys are on the table.
She lives in a small town near the coast.
examples.translation: O, kıyıya yakın küçük bir kasabada yaşıyor.

examples.sentence: Meet me at the entrance at 6 o'clock.
The cat is hiding under the bed.
There is a bookstore between the bank and the café.
examples.translation: Banka ile kafe arasında bir kitapçı var.

common_mistakes.wrong: I am in the bus now.
common_mistakes.correct: I am on the bus now.
common_mistakes.explanation: Public transport you can walk around in (bus, train, plane) uses 'on', not 'in', even though many languages use an equivalent of 'inside'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: İçinde yürüyerek dolaşabildiğiniz toplu taşıma araçlarında (otobüs, tren, uçak) 'on' kullanılır, 'in' değil; birçok dilde 'içinde' karşılığı kullanılsa da İngilizce'de bu farklıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: She arrived to the airport at 9 pm.
common_mistakes.correct: She arrived at the airport at 9 pm.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Arrive' is followed by 'at' (for a place/point) or 'in' (for a city/country), never by 'to'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Arrive' fiilinden sonra 'at' (bir nokta/mekan için) veya 'in' (şehir/ülke için) gelir, asla 'to' gelmez.

common_mistakes.wrong: He lives on Ankara.
common_mistakes.correct: He lives in Ankara.
common_mistakes.explanation: Cities and countries always take 'in', not 'on'; 'on' is reserved for streets/surfaces.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Şehir ve ülke isimleriyle her zaman 'in' kullanılır, 'on' değil; 'on' cadde/yüzey için ayrılmıştır.

common_mistakes.wrong: The picture is hanging in the wall.
common_mistakes.correct: The picture is hanging on the wall.
common_mistakes.explanation: For something attached to a vertical or horizontal surface, English uses 'on', not 'in'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Bir yüzeye (dikey veya yatay) tutturulmuş bir şey için İngilizce 'on' kullanır, 'in' değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: We will meet in the corner of the street.
common_mistakes.correct: We will meet at the corner of the street / on the corner of the street.
common_mistakes.explanation: A corner is treated as a specific point ('at') or a fixed surface location ('on' in American English), not an enclosed space ('in').
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Köşe, belirli bir nokta ('at') veya sabit bir yüzey konumu (Amerikan İngilizcesinde 'on') olarak ele alınır, kapalı bir alan ('in') olarak değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: The conference will be held ____ the Grand Hotel, which is located ____ Fifth Avenue.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Belirli bir mekan noktası için 'at the Grand Hotel', cadde için 'on Fifth Avenue' kullanılır.

toefl_style_questions.question: The novel is ____ the shelf, right ____ the two dictionaries.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Yüzey üzerindeki nesne için 'on the shelf'; iki nesne arasında olduğu için 'between' (among üçten fazla nesne için kullanılır).

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL frequently swaps in/on/at in transport, address, and city expressions, and tests between vs. among based on whether exactly two or more than two items are involved.

topics.title: Subject/Object Pronouns and Possessive Adjectives
topics.explanation: English pronouns change form depending on their grammatical role: subject pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they) perform the action; object pronouns (me, you, him, her, it, us, them) receive the action or follow a preposition; possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, its, our, their) show ownership and are always followed by a noun. Turkish learners often confuse these because Turkish pronoun/possessive marking works differently, especially with suffixes attached directly to the noun.
topics.explanation_tr: İngilizce zamirler, cümledeki görevine göre biçim değiştirir: özne zamirleri (I, you, he, she, it, we, they) eylemi yapar; nesne zamirleri (me, you, him, her, it, us, them) eylemi alır veya bir edattan sonra gelir; iyelik sıfatları (my, your, his, her, its, our, their) sahiplik gösterir ve her zaman bir isimden önce gelir. Türkçe'de iyelik doğrudan isme ek olarak eklendiği için Türk öğrenciler bu üç kategoriyi sık sık karıştırır.
structure_patterns: Verb/preposition + object pronoun (Give it to me.)
Possessive adjective + noun (This is my book.)
Possessive pronoun (mine/yours/his/hers/ours/theirs) — stands alone, no noun after it
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Bu üçlü (özne/nesne/iyelik) her zaman birlikte öğrenilmelidir çünkü aynı kişiye ait farklı görevlerdeki biçimlerdir.

exceptions.rule: 'It' and 'its' have no apostrophe in the possessive form, unlike the contraction 'it's' (= it is).
exceptions.example: The dog wagged its tail. (NOT: it's tail)
exceptions.explanation_tr: İyelik 'its' kesme işareti almaz; 'it's' ise 'it is' kısaltmasıdır, farklı bir şeydir.

exceptions.rule: After a preposition, English always uses the object pronoun, even when the pronoun looks like the subject of a following clause.
exceptions.example: Between you and me, this plan won't work. (NOT: between you and I)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Bir edattan sonra her zaman nesne zamiri kullanılır; 'between you and I' hem yaygın hem yanlıştır.

examples.sentence: He gave the book to her.
This is our house, not theirs.
I called him, but he didn't answer.
Is this pen yours or mine?
examples.translation: Bu kalem senin mi yoksa benim mi?

examples.sentence: The company changed its logo last year.

common_mistakes.wrong: Me and him went to the cinema.
common_mistakes.correct: He and I went to the cinema.
common_mistakes.explanation: Subject pronouns must be used for the subject of the sentence; object pronouns like 'me' cannot be the subject, and the order 'X and I' is conventional.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Cümlenin öznesi için özne zamirleri kullanılmalıdır; 'me' gibi nesne zamirleri özne olamaz. Ayrıca 'X and I' sıralaması geleneksel olarak tercih edilir.

common_mistakes.wrong: This is her car, not she car.
common_mistakes.correct: This is her car, not hers.
common_mistakes.explanation: A possessive pronoun (hers) stands alone without a noun; a possessive adjective (her) must be followed by a noun. Mixing subject pronoun 'she' into a possessive slot is also incorrect.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: İyelik zamiri (hers) tek başına kullanılır, isim gerekmez; iyelik sıfatı (her) her zaman bir isimle kullanılır. Özne zamiri 'she'nin iyelik yerine konması da yanlıştır.

common_mistakes.wrong: I saw she at the market yesterday.
common_mistakes.correct: I saw her at the market yesterday.
common_mistakes.explanation: As the object of the verb 'saw', the object pronoun 'her' is required, not the subject pronoun 'she'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Saw' fiilinin nesnesi olduğu için nesne zamiri 'her' gereklidir, özne zamiri 'she' değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: The dog is looking for it's bone.
common_mistakes.correct: The dog is looking for its bone.
common_mistakes.explanation: The possessive 'its' never takes an apostrophe; 'it's' with an apostrophe always means 'it is' or 'it has'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: İyelik 'its' asla kesme işareti almaz; kesme işaretli 'it's' her zaman 'it is' veya 'it has' anlamına gelir.

common_mistakes.wrong: This book of my is very interesting.
common_mistakes.correct: This book of mine is very interesting.
common_mistakes.explanation: After 'of', the possessive pronoun form (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) is required, not the possessive adjective (my, your...).
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Of'tan sonra iyelik zamiri (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) gerekir, iyelik sıfatı (my, your...) değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: The manager asked ____ to submit the report before ____ leaves for vacation.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Asked' fiilinin nesnesi olduğu için 'us' (nesne zamiri); ikinci boşlukta 'leaves' fiilinin öznesi olduğu için 'he' (özne zamiri) gerekir.

toefl_style_questions.question: The committee announced ____ decision after reviewing all of the candidates ____ submitted applications.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Committee' tekil bir kolektif isim olarak ele alınır, bu yüzden 'its' (kesme işaretsiz) gerekir; ikinci boşlukta özne göreviyle 'who' kullanılır.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL often embeds its/it's confusion and subject-vs-object pronoun choice inside longer, more formal sentences where the correct role of the pronoun is not obvious at first glance.

topics.title: There is / There are & Demonstratives (this/that/these/those)
topics.title_tr: There is / There are ve İşaret Zamirleri (this/that/these/those)
topics.explanation: 'There is/are' introduces the existence of something for the first time, with the verb agreeing with the noun that follows it, not with the word 'there' itself. Demonstratives (this, that, these, those) point to specific things based on singular/plural and near/far distinctions: this/these for things close to the speaker, that/those for things farther away.
topics.explanation_tr: 'There is/are', bir şeyin varlığını ilk kez tanıtır; fiil 'there' kelimesiyle değil, ondan sonra gelen isimle uyumlanır. İşaret zamirleri (this, that, these, those) tekil/çoğul ve yakın/uzak ayrımına göre belirli şeylere işaret eder: konuşana yakın olanlar için this/these, daha uzak olanlar için that/those kullanılır.
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'There is/are' varlık bildirirken, 'this/that/these/those' belirli bir nesneyi işaret ederken kullanılır; ikisi karıştırılmamalıdır.

exceptions.rule: With two or more nouns joined by 'and' after 'there is/are', the verb often agrees with the closest noun in informal speech.
exceptions.example: There is a book and two pens on the desk. (informal, agrees with 'a book')
exceptions.explanation_tr: Gündelik konuşmada 'there is/are'den sonra 'and' ile bağlanan birden fazla isim varsa, fiil genellikle en yakın isimle uyumlanır.

exceptions.rule: 'That' (not 'this') is used to refer back to something already mentioned or agreed upon, even if it was mentioned only a moment ago.
exceptions.example: A: I got the job! B: That's great news!
exceptions.explanation_tr: Az önce söylenmiş bir şeye atıfta bulunurken 'this' değil 'that' kullanılır.

examples.sentence: There is a problem with the printer.
There are many reasons to learn English.
examples.translation: İngilizce öğrenmek için birçok sebep var.

examples.sentence: This coffee is too hot to drink.
examples.translation: Bu kahve içmek için çok sıcak.

examples.sentence: Those mountains in the distance are beautiful.
Is there a bank near here?
examples.translation: Buraya yakın bir banka var mı?

common_mistakes.wrong: There is many students in the classroom.
common_mistakes.correct: There are many students in the classroom.
common_mistakes.explanation: The verb must agree with 'students' (plural), not stay fixed as 'is'; learners often treat 'there is' as a frozen phrase.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Fiil 'students' (çoğul) ile uyumlanmalıdır, 'is' olarak sabit kalmamalıdır; öğrenciler genellikle 'there is'i donmuş bir ifade gibi kullanır.

common_mistakes.wrong: It has a book on the table.
common_mistakes.correct: There is a book on the table.
common_mistakes.explanation: To express existence, English requires 'there is/are', not 'it has', which is a direct (incorrect) translation pattern from some other languages.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Varlık bildirmek için İngilizce 'there is/are' gerektirir, 'it has' değil; bu, bazı dillerden yapılan doğrudan (hatalı) çeviri kalıbıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: This books are expensive.
common_mistakes.correct: These books are expensive.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'This' is only for singular nouns; the plural demonstrative 'these' must be used with plural nouns.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'This' sadece tekil isimlerle kullanılır; çoğul isimlerle çoğul işaret zamiri 'these' kullanılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: There aren't no problems with the plan.
common_mistakes.correct: There aren't any problems with the plan. / There are no problems with the plan.
common_mistakes.explanation: Standard English does not use double negatives; either 'aren't ... any' or 'are ... no' is correct, not both negatives together.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Standart İngilizce'de çift olumsuzluk kullanılmaz; ya 'aren't ... any' ya da 'are ... no' doğrudur, ikisi birlikte kullanılmaz.

common_mistakes.wrong: That people over here are my colleagues.
common_mistakes.correct: Those people over there are my colleagues.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'That' is singular and typically pairs with 'over there' (far), while plural 'people' requires 'those'; mixing singular/plural demonstratives with plural nouns is a common slip.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'That' tekildir ve genellikle 'over there' (uzak) ile eşleşir; çoğul 'people' isminden önce çoğul işaret zamiri 'those' gerekir.

toefl_style_questions.question: ____ several factors that contributed to the company's rapid growth last year.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Several factors' çoğul olduğu için 'there are' kullanılır.

toefl_style_questions.question: ____ findings, published last month, challenge ____ theory that was widely accepted for decades.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Findings' çoğul olduğu için 'these'; 'theory' tekil olduğu için 'that' kullanılır.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL frequently checks whether 'there is/are' agrees with the noun that follows it, and whether demonstrative pronouns match the number (singular/plural) of the noun they modify.

topics.title: Past Simple
topics.explanation: The past simple describes completed actions or situations at a specific, finished point in the past. Regular verbs add -ed; irregular verbs (go→went, have→had, see→saw) change form unpredictably and must be memorized. Negatives and questions use 'did/didn't', after which the main verb always returns to its base form.
topics.explanation_tr: Past simple, geçmişte belirli ve bitmiş bir zamanda gerçekleşen tamamlanmış eylem veya durumları anlatır. Düzenli fiiller -ed alır; düzensiz fiiller (go→went, have→had, see→saw) tahmin edilemez şekilde değişir ve ezberlenmelidir. Olumsuz ve soru cümlelerinde 'did/didn't' kullanılır; bu durumda ana fiil her zaman yalın haline döner.
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Bu zaman belirteçleri geçmişte tamamlanmış, belirli bir noktayı işaret eder ve present perfect ile karıştırılmamalıdır.

exceptions.rule: Verbs ending in -e just add -d.
exceptions.example: live → lived, like → liked
exceptions.explanation_tr: -e ile bitn fiillere sadece -d eklenir.

exceptions.rule: One-syllable verbs ending in a single vowel + consonant double the final consonant before -ed.
exceptions.example: stop → stopped, plan → planned
exceptions.explanation_tr: Tek heceli, tek sesli harf + sessiz harfle biten fiillerde son sessiz harf ikilenir.

exceptions.rule: 'Used to' + base verb expresses past habits or states that no longer exist, a special structure distinct from simple past.
exceptions.example: I used to smoke, but I quit two years ago.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Used to' geçmişteki alışkanlık veya durumları, artık geçerli olmadığını vurgulayarak anlatır; simple past'ten ayrı bir yapıdır.

examples.sentence: I visited my grandmother last weekend.
examples.translation: Geçen hafta sonu büyükannemi ziyaret ettim.

examples.sentence: She didn't call me yesterday.
Did you finish your homework?
They went to Paris two years ago.
He was born in 1998.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have seen him yesterday.
common_mistakes.correct: I saw him yesterday.
common_mistakes.explanation: A specific finished-time expression like 'yesterday' requires simple past, not present perfect.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Yesterday' gibi belirli bitmiş zaman ifadeleri simple past gerektirir, present perfect değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: She didn't went to school.
common_mistakes.correct: She didn't go to school.
common_mistakes.explanation: Once 'did/didn't' appears, the main verb must be in the base form; adding the past form again is a very common double-marking error.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Did/didn't' geldiğinde ana fiil yalın halde olmalıdır; fiili tekrar geçmiş zaman yapmak çok yaygın bir çift işaretleme hatasıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: I goed to the market.
common_mistakes.correct: I went to the market.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Go' is irregular (go→went); adding the regular -ed ending to an irregular verb is a classic overgeneralization mistake.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Go' düzensiz bir fiildir (go→went); düzensiz bir fiile düzenli -ed eki eklemek klasik bir aşırı genelleme hatasıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: Where did you went last night?
common_mistakes.correct: Where did you go last night?
common_mistakes.explanation: After the auxiliary 'did' in a question, the main verb must stay in base form, not past form.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Sorudaki 'did' yardımcı fiilinden sonra ana fiil yalın halde kalmalıdır, geçmiş zaman biçiminde değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: I no went to the party.
common_mistakes.correct: I didn't go to the party.
common_mistakes.explanation: Negation in past simple must use 'didn't', not 'no', which is a direct translation pattern from other languages.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Past simple'da olumsuzluk 'didn't' ile yapılır, 'no' ile değil; bu, başka dillerden yapılan doğrudan çeviri kalıbıdır.

toefl_style_questions.question: The committee ____ its final decision after a long debate last Tuesday.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Last Tuesday' belirli bir geçmiş zaman noktasıdır, bu yüzden simple past ('made') kullanılır.

toefl_style_questions.question: How many candidates ____ for the position before the deadline?
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Soruda özne olarak 'how many candidates' kullanıldığında 'did' gerekmez; asıl fiil doğrudan past simple alır.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL frequently tests whether past simple is confused with present perfect when a specific past time marker (yesterday, in 1990, last year) is present, and checks irregular verb forms.

topics.title: Present Continuous
topics.explanation: The present continuous (am/is/are + V-ing) describes actions happening right now, temporary situations, and pre-arranged future plans. It contrasts sharply with present simple, which describes habits rather than in-progress actions — a distinction that does not exist grammatically in Turkish the same way.
topics.explanation_tr: Present continuous (am/is/are + V-ing), şu anda gerçekleşen eylemleri, geçici durumları ve önceden planlanmış gelecek düzenlemelerini anlatır. Alışkanlıkları değil, süregelen eylemleri anlatan present simple'dan net bir şekilde ayrılır; bu ayrım Türkçe'de aynı şekilde dilbilgisel olarak yoktur.
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Bu ifadeler eylemin konuşma anında sürdüğünü ya da geçici olarak devam ettiğini gösterir.

exceptions.rule: Stative verbs (know, believe, like, want, need, understand, own) are not normally used in continuous form.
exceptions.example: I understand the lesson. (NOT: I am understanding the lesson.)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Durum fiilleri (know, believe, like, want, need, understand, own) genellikle continuous formda kullanılmaz.

exceptions.rule: Present continuous can express a fixed future arrangement, especially with a future time expression.
exceptions.example: I'm meeting my dentist at 3 pm tomorrow.
exceptions.explanation_tr: Present continuous, özellikle gelecek zaman ifadesiyle birlikte, kesinleşmiş bir gelecek planını da anlatabilir.

examples.sentence: She is studying for her exam right now.
We are having dinner with friends tonight.
Are you listening to me?
He isn't working today; he's on holiday.
Prices are rising rapidly these days.

common_mistakes.wrong: I am knowing the answer.
common_mistakes.correct: I know the answer.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and does not take the continuous form, even to emphasize the present moment.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Know' bir durum fiilidir ve şu anı vurgulamak için bile continuous form almaz.

common_mistakes.wrong: She work in London this month.
common_mistakes.correct: She is working in London this month.
common_mistakes.explanation: A temporary, time-limited situation ('this month') requires present continuous, not present simple.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Sınırlı bir süre için geçerli, geçici bir durum ('this month') present continuous gerektirir, present simple değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: Look! The dog run to the door.
common_mistakes.correct: Look! The dog is running to the door.
common_mistakes.explanation: The signal word 'look!' points to an action happening right now, which requires -ing, not the base/simple form.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Look!' sinyal kelimesi şu anda olan bir eylemi işaret eder; bu yüzden -ing formu gerekir, yalın/simple form değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: He is having a car.
common_mistakes.correct: He has a car.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Have' meaning possession is stative and stays in simple form; only 'have' as an action (having a meal/having a good time) can be continuous.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Sahiplik anlamındaki 'have' durum fiilidir ve simple formda kalır; sadece bir eylem anlamındaki 'have' (yemek yemek, iyi zaman geçirmek) continuous olabilir.

common_mistakes.wrong: I am agreeing with your opinion.
common_mistakes.correct: I agree with your opinion.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Agree' expresses a mental state, not an ongoing physical action, so it stays in the simple form.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Agree' fiziksel bir eylem değil, zihinsel bir durum ifade eder; bu yüzden simple formda kalır.

toefl_style_questions.question: Scientists ____ a new vaccine at the moment, and early results look promising.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'At the moment' şu anda süren bir eylemi gösterir, bu yüzden present continuous kullanılır.

toefl_style_questions.question: I'm afraid I ____ with you on this issue; the evidence points the other way.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Agree' durum fiilidir, continuous formda kullanılmaz; olumsuzu 'don't agree' şeklindedir.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests stative verbs wrongly placed in continuous form, and checks whether temporary vs. permanent situations correctly trigger continuous vs. simple present.

topics.title: Comparatives and Superlatives
topics.explanation: Comparatives compare two things (bigger, more interesting, less expensive) and are typically followed by 'than'; superlatives single out the extreme within a group of three or more (the biggest, the most interesting) and are usually preceded by 'the'. Short adjectives (1 syllable, or 2 syllables ending in -y) add -er/-est; longer adjectives use more/most instead.
topics.explanation_tr: Karşılaştırma sıfatları (bigger, more interesting, less expensive) iki şeyi karşılaştırır ve genellikle 'than' ile kullanılır; üstünlük sıfatları (the biggest, the most interesting) üç veya daha fazla şey arasında en uç noktayı belirtir ve genellikle önüne 'the' alır. Kısa sıfatlar (1 hece veya -y ile biten 2 hece) -er/-est alır; uzun sıfatlar more/most kullanır.
structure_patterns: S + V + more/less + adjective + than + noun
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'Than' karşılaştırma sinyalidir; 'the ... in/of (a group)' üstünlük sinyalidir.

exceptions.rule: Some common adjectives are irregular: good→better→best, bad→worse→worst, far→farther/further→farthest/furthest.
exceptions.example: This is the best solution we have found so far.
exceptions.explanation_tr: Bazı yaygın sıfatlar düzensizdir: good→better→best, bad→worse→worst, far→farther/further→farthest/furthest.

exceptions.rule: Adjectives ending in a single vowel + consonant double the consonant before -er/-est.
exceptions.example: big → bigger → biggest
exceptions.explanation_tr: Tek sesli harf + sessiz harfle biten sıfatlarda -er/-est'ten önce sessiz harf ikilenir.

exceptions.rule: 'As + adjective + as' expresses equality, not comparison in the usual sense.
exceptions.example: She is as tall as her brother.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'As + sıfat + as' eşitlik ifade eder, klasik karşılaştırma değildir.

examples.sentence: This phone is cheaper than that one.
examples.translation: Bu telefon o telefondan daha ucuz.

examples.sentence: She is the most talented singer in her school.
Traveling by train is more comfortable than traveling by bus.
examples.translation: Trenle seyahat etmek otobüsle seyahat etmekten daha rahat.

examples.sentence: He is not as tall as his father.
This was the worst movie I have ever seen.

common_mistakes.wrong: This book is more good than that one.
common_mistakes.correct: This book is better than that one.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Good' has the irregular comparative 'better'; combining 'more' with an irregular adjective is a common overgeneralization.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Good' düzensiz karşılaştırma biçimi olan 'better'ı alır; düzensiz bir sıfatla 'more' kullanmak yaygın bir aşırı genelleme hatasıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: She is the more intelligent student in the class.
common_mistakes.correct: She is the most intelligent student in the class.
common_mistakes.explanation: When comparing within a group of three or more (the whole class), the superlative form is required, not the comparative.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Üç veya daha fazla kişi/şey arasında karşılaştırma yapılırken (bütün sınıf) üstünlük biçimi gerekir, karşılaştırma biçimi değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: He is more taller than me.
common_mistakes.correct: He is taller than me/I.
common_mistakes.explanation: Short adjectives take only one comparative marker (-er); using both '-er' and 'more' together is a double marking error.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Kısa sıfatlar sadece bir karşılaştırma işareti alır (-er); '-er' ve 'more'u birlikte kullanmak çift işaretleme hatasıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: This is the most beautifulest city I have visited.
common_mistakes.correct: This is the most beautiful city I have visited.
common_mistakes.explanation: Longer adjectives use only 'most', not both '-est' and 'most' together.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Uzun sıfatlar sadece 'most' alır; '-est' ve 'most'u birlikte kullanmak yanlıştır.

common_mistakes.wrong: She is as taller as her sister.
common_mistakes.correct: She is as tall as her sister.
common_mistakes.explanation: In the 'as ... as' equality structure, the base adjective form is used, not the comparative form.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'As ... as' eşitlik yapısında sıfatın yalın hali kullanılır, karşılaştırma biçimi değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: Renewable energy sources are becoming ____ than fossil fuels in many countries.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Kısa bir sıfat olan 'cheap' -er alır ve 'than' ile birlikte kullanılır.

toefl_style_questions.question: Of all the candidates, she has ____ experience in international law.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Of all the candidates' bir grup içindeki en üst düzeyi belirtir; bu yüzden üstünlük biçimi 'the most' gerekir.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests irregular comparatives/superlatives (good/better/best), double comparative marking, and whether the correct form (comparative vs. superlative) matches a 'than' clue vs. a group/'of all' clue.

topics.title: Countable and Uncountable Nouns
topics.explanation: Countable nouns can be counted individually and have both singular and plural forms (a book, two books). Uncountable nouns describe substances, concepts, or categories that are not divided into separate units and have no plural form (water, information, advice, furniture). Quantifiers differ for each type: many/few/several for countable, much/little/a great deal of for uncountable, and 'some/any/a lot of' for both.
topics.explanation_tr: Sayılabilir isimler tek tek sayılabilir ve tekil/çoğul biçimleri vardır (a book, two books). Sayılamaz isimler madde, kavram veya kategori bildirir, ayrı birimlere bölünmez ve çoğul biçimleri yoktur (water, information, advice, furniture). Miktar belirteçleri her iki türde farklıdır: sayılabilir için many/few/several, sayılamaz için much/little/a great deal of, ve her ikisi için 'some/any/a lot of' kullanılır.
structure_patterns: many/few/several/a number of + countable plural noun
much/little/a great deal of + uncountable noun
some/any/a lot of/plenty of + either type
a piece of/a bottle of/a bit of + uncountable noun (unitizing)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'Many/few' sayılabilir isimlerle, 'much/little' sayılamaz isimlerle kullanılır; bu ayrım TOEFL'da sıkça test edilir.

exceptions.rule: Some nouns that are countable in Turkish are uncountable in English: information, advice, news, furniture, luggage/baggage, equipment, homework, traffic.
exceptions.example: The news was shocking. (singular verb, no plural 'newses')
exceptions.explanation_tr: Türkçe'de sayılabilir görünen bazı isimler İngilizce'de sayılamazdır: information, advice, news, furniture, luggage/baggage, equipment, homework, traffic.

exceptions.rule: Some nouns can be both countable and uncountable with a change in meaning.
exceptions.example: I'd like a coffee (a cup). / Coffee is grown in Brazil (the substance in general).
exceptions.explanation_tr: Bazı isimler anlam değişimiyle hem sayılabilir hem sayılamaz olarak kullanılabilir: 'a coffee' (bir fincan) vs 'coffee' (genel madde).

examples.sentence: How much money do you have with you?
There aren't many chairs in this room.
examples.translation: Bu odada çok fazla sandalye yok.

examples.sentence: She gave me some useful advice.
We need a few more volunteers for the event.
examples.translation: Etkinlik için birkaç gönüllüye daha ihtiyacımız var.

examples.sentence: I bought a bottle of water and two loaves of bread.
examples.translation: Bir şişe su ve iki somun ekmek aldım.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have many homeworks today.
common_mistakes.correct: I have a lot of homework today.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Homework' is uncountable in English and has no plural; 'many' also cannot be used with an uncountable noun.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Homework' İngilizce'de sayılamazdır ve çoğulu yoktur; 'many' de sayılamaz bir isimle kullanılamaz.

common_mistakes.wrong: How much books did you buy?
common_mistakes.correct: How many books did you buy?
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Books' is countable and plural, so it requires 'many', not 'much', which is reserved for uncountable nouns.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Books' sayılabilir ve çoğuldur; bu yüzden sayılamaz isimlere ayrılan 'much' değil, 'many' gerekir.

common_mistakes.wrong: She gave me an advice about my career.
common_mistakes.correct: She gave me some advice / a piece of advice about my career.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable and cannot take 'a/an'; a unit like 'a piece of' must be used to individualize it if needed.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Advice' sayılamazdır ve 'a/an' alamaz; gerekirse bireyselleştirmek için 'a piece of' gibi bir birim kullanılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: There is a little chairs in the office.
common_mistakes.correct: There are a few chairs / not many chairs in the office.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Chairs' is countable, so 'a few' (not 'a little', which is for uncountable nouns) should be used, and the verb must agree (are, not is).
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Chairs' sayılabilir olduğu için sayılamaz isimlere ayrılan 'a little' değil 'a few' kullanılmalıdır; fiil de uyumlu olmalıdır (are, is değil).

common_mistakes.wrong: His furnitures are very old.
common_mistakes.correct: His furniture is very old.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable collective noun in English with no plural form and takes a singular verb.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Furniture' İngilizce'de çoğulu olmayan sayılamaz bir toplu isimdir ve tekil fiil alır.

toefl_style_questions.question: Despite ____ evidence supporting the theory, ____ scientists still remain skeptical.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Evidence' sayılamaz bir isimdir → 'much'; 'scientists' sayılabilir ve çoğuldur → 'a few'.

toefl_style_questions.question: The report contained very ____ useful information, so we had to gather ____ additional data.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Information' ve 'data' sayılamaz isimlerdir, bu yüzden 'little' ve 'much' kullanılır.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL heavily tests nouns that differ in countability between English and other languages (information, advice, news, furniture, data) paired with many/much or few/little.

topics.title: Modals of Ability (can/could)
topics.explanation: 'Can' expresses present ability, permission, or possibility; 'could' expresses past ability, polite requests, or hypothetical possibility. Modal verbs never change form for different subjects (no -s, no -ing, no -ed) and are always followed directly by the base form of the main verb, without 'to'.
topics.explanation_tr: 'Can' şimdiki zamanda yetenek, izin veya olasılık; 'could' geçmişte yetenek, kibar rica veya varsayımsal olasılık ifade eder. Modal fiiller özneye göre biçim değiştirmez (-s, -ing, -ed almaz) ve her zaman doğrudan ana fiilin yalın haliyle kullanılır, aralarına 'to' girmez.
structure_patterns: S + be able to + V(base) (alternative for other tenses)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'Could', geçmiş genel yetenek anlatırken kullanılır ama tek bir seferlik başarılı eylem için genellikle 'was/were able to' tercih edilir.

exceptions.rule: For a single, specific past achievement (not a general ability), 'was/were able to' is preferred over 'could'.
exceptions.example: After years of training, she was able to finish the marathon. (NOT usually: she could finish)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Genel bir yetenek değil, tek seferlik özel bir başarı anlatılırken 'could' yerine genellikle 'was/were able to' tercih edilir.

exceptions.rule: Modal verbs have no infinitive or -ing form; to express ability in other tenses, 'be able to' must be used.
exceptions.example: I would like to be able to speak Japanese fluently.
exceptions.explanation_tr: Modal fiillerin mastar veya -ing hali yoktur; diğer zamanlarda yeteneği ifade etmek için 'be able to' kullanılmalıdır.

examples.sentence: She can swim very well.
When I was young, I could run for hours.
Could you help me with this box, please?
examples.translation: Bu kutuyla bana yardım eder misiniz lütfen?

examples.sentence: He can't come to the meeting tomorrow.
We will be able to finish the project by Friday.

common_mistakes.wrong: She can to speak three languages.
common_mistakes.correct: She can speak three languages.
common_mistakes.explanation: Modal verbs like 'can' are followed directly by the base verb without 'to'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Can' gibi modal fiillerden sonra ana fiil doğrudan gelir, araya 'to' girmez.

common_mistakes.wrong: He cans play the piano.
common_mistakes.correct: He can play the piano.
common_mistakes.explanation: Modal verbs never take an -s ending, even with he/she/it.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Modal fiiller he/she/it ile de asla -s eki almaz.

common_mistakes.wrong: I could to finish the marathon last year.
common_mistakes.correct: I was able to finish the marathon last year.
common_mistakes.explanation: For a single specific past success, 'was/were able to' is more natural than 'could'; also 'could' should never be followed by 'to'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Tek seferlik özel bir geçmiş başarı için 'could' yerine 'was/were able to' daha doğaldır; ayrıca 'could'dan sonra asla 'to' gelmez.

common_mistakes.wrong: In the future, I can to be a good doctor if I study hard.
common_mistakes.correct: In the future, I will be able to be a good doctor if I study hard.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Can' has no future form; 'will be able to' must be used to express future ability, and 'to' never follows a modal directly.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Can'in gelecek zaman hali yoktur; gelecekteki yeteneği ifade etmek için 'will be able to' kullanılmalıdır; ayrıca modalden sonra doğrudan 'to' gelmez.

common_mistakes.wrong: Can you to open the window, please?
common_mistakes.correct: Can you open the window, please?
common_mistakes.explanation: Even in polite requests, 'can/could' is followed directly by the base verb, with no 'to' in between.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Kibar ricalarda da 'can/could'dan sonra doğrudan ana fiil gelir, araya 'to' girmez.

toefl_style_questions.question: Before the new policy was introduced, employees ____ take unlimited sick days.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Geçmişte var olan genel bir yetenek/izin anlatıldığı için 'could' kullanılır.

toefl_style_questions.question: Thanks to the new software, the team ____ complete the analysis in half the usual time.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Can'in başka bir yardımcı fiille (is) birleşik kullanımı yanlıştır; şimdiki zamanda yetenek için doğrudan 'is able to' kullanılabilir.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests the impossible combination of a modal + 'to' + verb, and checks whether 'could' vs. 'was able to' is chosen correctly for general ability vs. a single achievement.

topics.title: Past Continuous
topics.explanation: The past continuous (was/were + V-ing) describes an action that was in progress at a specific moment in the past, often interrupted by another shorter action expressed in past simple. It is also used for two simultaneous background actions in the past, and to set the scene in narratives.
topics.explanation_tr: Past continuous (was/were + V-ing), geçmişte belirli bir anda sürmekte olan bir eylemi anlatır ve genellikle past simple ile ifade edilen daha kısa bir eylem tarafından kesilir. Ayrıca geçmişte eş zamanlı iki arka plan eylemini anlatmak ve anlatılarda sahneyi kurmak için de kullanılır.
structure_patterns: S + was/were + V-ing + when + S + V-ed (interruption)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'While' genellikle iki sürekli eylemi bağlar; 'when' ise genellikle sürekli bir eylemi kesen ani bir eylemi bağlar.

exceptions.rule: 'While' typically introduces the longer, background action (past continuous); 'when' typically introduces the shorter, interrupting action (past simple).
exceptions.example: While I was cooking, the phone rang.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'While' genellikle daha uzun, arka plan eylemi (past continuous) başlatır; 'when' genellikle daha kısa, kesen eylemi (past simple) başlatır.

exceptions.rule: Stative verbs are not usually used in past continuous, just as in present continuous.
exceptions.example: I knew the answer. (NOT: I was knowing the answer.)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Durum fiilleri present continuous'ta olduğu gibi past continuous'ta da genelde kullanılmaz.

examples.sentence: I was reading a book when you called.
They were watching TV while I was doing my homework.
examples.translation: Ben ödevimi yaparken onlar televizyon izliyordu.

examples.sentence: What were you doing at 8 pm last night?
She wasn't paying attention during the lecture.
It was raining heavily when we left the house.

common_mistakes.wrong: While I cooked dinner, the phone rang.
common_mistakes.correct: While I was cooking dinner, the phone rang.
common_mistakes.explanation: The background, longer action after 'while' should be in past continuous, not past simple, to show it was already in progress.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'While'dan sonra gelen daha uzun, arka plan eylemi, zaten sürmekte olduğunu göstermek için past continuous'ta olmalıdır, past simple'da değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: I was knowing him for many years before we became friends.
common_mistakes.correct: I had known him for many years before we became friends.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Know' is stative and does not take continuous form; also, for a state continuing up to a past point, past perfect is more appropriate here.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Know' durum fiilidir ve continuous form almaz; ayrıca geçmişteki bir noktaya kadar süren bir durum için past perfect daha uygundur.

common_mistakes.wrong: When I was walking home, I was seeing an accident.
common_mistakes.correct: When I was walking home, I saw an accident.
common_mistakes.explanation: The short, completed interrupting event should be in past simple, not past continuous, even though the background action stays continuous.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Kısa, tamamlanmış kesen olay past simple'da olmalıdır, past continuous'ta değil; arka plan eylemi ise continuous kalır.

common_mistakes.wrong: She was always studying when she was young, so she was becoming a doctor.
common_mistakes.correct: She always studied when she was young, so she became a doctor.
common_mistakes.explanation: Repeated habitual past actions and single completed results should be expressed with past simple, not past continuous.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Tekrarlanan alışılmış geçmiş eylemler ve tek bir tamamlanmış sonuç past simple ile ifade edilmelidir, past continuous ile değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: At 9 pm last night, I was arrive home.
common_mistakes.correct: At 9 pm last night, I was arriving home. / I arrived home at 9 pm last night.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Was' must be followed by the -ing form for continuous, not the base form; alternatively, past simple can be used to describe the completed arrival.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Was'tan sonra continuous için -ing formu gelmelidir, yalın form değil; alternatif olarak tamamlanmış varışı anlatmak için past simple kullanılabilir.

toefl_style_questions.question: The lights suddenly went out while the audience ____ the final act of the play.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Audience' burada tekil bir grup olarak ele alınmış ve 'while' ile birlikte devam eden bir eylemi anlatır: was watching.

toefl_style_questions.question: I ____ for my keys when I finally found them in my coat pocket.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'When I finally found them' kesen kısa eylemdir (past simple); arama eylemi arka planda sürdüğü için past continuous kullanılır.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL checks whether the longer background action correctly takes past continuous while the short interrupting action correctly takes past simple, especially around 'while' and 'when'.

topics.title: Future with 'going to'
topics.explanation: 'Be going to' + base verb expresses future plans and intentions decided before the moment of speaking, as well as predictions based on present evidence. It contrasts with 'will', which is often used for spontaneous decisions, promises, or general predictions without present evidence.
topics.explanation_tr: 'Be going to' + yalın fiil, konuşma anından önce karar verilmiş gelecek plan ve niyetleri, ayrıca şimdiki kanıta dayanan tahminleri anlatır. Genellikle ani kararlar, sözler veya kanıta dayanmayan genel tahminler için kullanılan 'will' ile karşıtlık oluşturur.
structure_patterns: S + am/is/are + not + going to + V(base)
S + am/is/are + going to + V(base) (prediction with present evidence)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'Going to', karar konuşma öncesinde verilmişse ve/veya gözle görülür bir kanıt varsa tercih edilir.

exceptions.rule: In informal spoken English, 'going to' is often reduced to 'gonna', but this should not be used in formal writing (including TOEFL).
exceptions.example: I'm gonna call you later. (informal only)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Gündelik konuşmada 'going to' genelde 'gonna' olarak kısaltılır, ancak bu resmi yazıda (TOEFL dahil) kullanılmamalıdır.

exceptions.rule: With the verb 'go' itself, 'going to go' is often simplified to just 'going'.
exceptions.example: I'm going to the cinema tonight. (= I'm going to go to the cinema)
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Go' fiiliyle birlikte 'going to go' genellikle sadece 'going' olarak sadeleştirilir.

examples.sentence: I am going to study medicine at university.
Look at those dark clouds — it's going to rain.
examples.translation: O kara bulutlara bak — yağmur yağacak.

examples.sentence: Are you going to attend the conference next week?
She isn't going to accept the job offer.
We are going to move to a new apartment in June.

common_mistakes.wrong: I will study medicine; I decided it last month.
common_mistakes.correct: I am going to study medicine; I decided it last month.
common_mistakes.explanation: Since the decision was already made before speaking, 'going to' is more accurate than 'will', which suggests a decision made at the moment of speaking.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Karar konuşmadan önce verildiği için, konuşma anında verilen kararı ima eden 'will' yerine 'going to' daha doğrudur.

common_mistakes.wrong: She is going study abroad next year.
common_mistakes.correct: She is going to study abroad next year.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'To' is an essential part of the structure 'going to + verb' and is frequently dropped by learners.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'To', 'going to + fiil' yapısının vazgeçilmez bir parçasıdır ve öğrenciler tarafından sık sık atlanır.

common_mistakes.wrong: It going to rain soon.
common_mistakes.correct: It is going to rain soon.
common_mistakes.explanation: The auxiliary 'to be' (is/am/are) must appear before 'going to'; it cannot be omitted even in short predictive sentences.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'To be' (is/am/are) yardımcı fiili 'going to'dan önce mutlaka bulunmalıdır; kısa tahmin cümlelerinde bile atlanamaz.

common_mistakes.wrong: We are going to went to the beach tomorrow.
common_mistakes.correct: We are going to go to the beach tomorrow.
common_mistakes.explanation: After 'going to', the main verb must stay in the base form; using a past form here is a mixing of two different tense markers.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Going to'dan sonra ana fiil yalın halde kalmalıdır; burada geçmiş zaman biçimi kullanmak iki farklı zaman işaretini karıştırmaktır.

common_mistakes.wrong: Are you going to studying tonight?
common_mistakes.correct: Are you going to study tonight?
common_mistakes.explanation: After 'going to', the base form of the verb is required, not the -ing form, which learners sometimes add by analogy with continuous tenses.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Going to'dan sonra fiilin yalın hali gerekir, continuous zamanlarla benzeşim kurularak eklenen -ing formu değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: Based on the latest sales figures, the company ____ open three new branches next year.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Mevcut kanıta (satış rakamlarına) dayanan bir tahmin için 'going to' kullanılır ve 'to be' (is) atlanamaz.

toefl_style_questions.question: We had already booked our flights months ago, so we ____ to Italy this summer regardless of the weather.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Önceden yapılmış bir plan/rezervasyon anlatıldığı için 'going to' yapısı (burada kısaltılmış hâliyle 'are going') uygundur.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests whether a pre-decided plan or visible-evidence prediction correctly uses 'going to' rather than 'will', and checks for a missing 'to be' or dropped 'to'.

topics.title: Adverbs of Frequency and Word Order
topics.explanation: Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) describe how often something happens and have a fixed position in the sentence: before the main verb, but after the verb 'to be' and after auxiliary verbs. Getting this word order wrong is one of the most persistent errors for learners whose native language places such adverbs elsewhere.
topics.explanation_tr: Sıklık zarfları (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) bir şeyin ne sıklıkla olduğunu anlatır ve cümlede sabit bir konuma sahiptir: ana fiilden önce, ama 'to be' fiilinden ve yardımcı fiillerden sonra gelir. Bu kelime sırasını yanlış yapmak, ana dilinde bu zarfları başka bir yere koyan öğrenciler için en kalıcı hatalardan biridir.
structure_patterns: frequency adverb (sometimes/usually/often) + S + V (sentence-initial, for emphasis)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Bu zarfların cümledeki konumu anlamı değil doğruluğu belirler; yanlış yer TOEFL'da doğrudan test edilir.

exceptions.rule: 'Sometimes', 'usually', 'often', and 'occasionally' can also go at the very beginning or end of a sentence for emphasis, unlike 'always/never/rarely/seldom', which stay in mid-position.
exceptions.example: Sometimes I forget to lock the door. / I forget to lock the door sometimes.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Sometimes, usually, often, occasionally' cümle başında veya sonunda da vurgu için kullanılabilir; 'always/never/rarely/seldom' genelde orta konumda kalır.

exceptions.rule: 'Rarely', 'seldom', and 'never' at the very start of a sentence trigger inversion (subject-verb order reversal) in formal writing.
exceptions.example: Rarely have I seen such dedication.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Rarely, seldom, never' cümle başına geldiğinde resmi yazıda devrik yapı (inversion) tetikler.

examples.sentence: I usually wake up at 7 am.
She is always late for meetings.
examples.translation: O toplantılara her zaman geç kalır.

examples.sentence: We have never visited that museum.
He rarely eats fast food.
They can sometimes be seen jogging in the park.

common_mistakes.wrong: I always am tired after work.
common_mistakes.correct: I am always tired after work.
common_mistakes.explanation: With 'to be', the frequency adverb goes after the verb, not before it, unlike with regular main verbs.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'To be' ile sıklık zarfı fiilden önce değil sonra gelir; bu, sıradan fiillerden farklıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: She usually is happy in the morning.
common_mistakes.correct: She is usually happy in the morning.
common_mistakes.explanation: The frequency adverb must come after 'is', not before it, since 'to be' is the verb here.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Sıklık zarfı 'is'ten önce değil sonra gelmelidir, çünkü burada fiil 'to be'dir.

common_mistakes.wrong: He never has finished his homework on time.
common_mistakes.correct: He has never finished his homework on time.
common_mistakes.explanation: With auxiliary verbs like 'has', the frequency adverb goes after the auxiliary and before the main verb, not before the auxiliary.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Has' gibi yardımcı fiillerle sıklık zarfı, yardımcı fiilden önce değil, yardımcı fiilden sonra ve ana fiilden önce gelir.

common_mistakes.wrong: Often I go to the gym after work.
common_mistakes.correct: I often go to the gym after work.
common_mistakes.explanation: While 'often' can appear at the start for strong emphasis, in neutral statements it should be placed in mid-position before the main verb, which is the safer default for learners.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Often' güçlü bir vurgu için başta da kullanılabilir, ama nötr cümlelerde öğrenciler için daha güvenli varsayılan konum ana fiilden önceki orta konumdur.

common_mistakes.wrong: Never I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
common_mistakes.correct: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
common_mistakes.explanation: When 'never' starts a sentence for emphasis, it requires subject-auxiliary inversion (have I, not I have).
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Never' vurgu için cümle başına geldiğinde özne-yardımcı fiil devrik yapısı gerekir (have I, I have değil).

toefl_style_questions.question: The results of the experiment ____ match the researchers' initial predictions.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Yardımcı fiil 'don't'tan sonra sıklık zarfı 'always' gelir, öncesinde değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: ____ has the committee received such a large number of applications for a single position.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Never' vurgulu bir şekilde cümle başına geldiğinde devrik yapı (has the committee) tetikler; 'never before' doğal bir birliktelik oluşturur.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests the fixed mid-position of frequency adverbs relative to 'to be' and auxiliary verbs, and occasionally tests the inversion triggered by 'never/rarely/seldom' at the start of a sentence.

topics.title: Present Perfect
topics.explanation: Present perfect (have/has + past participle) connects the past to the present: it is used for life experiences without a specific time, unfinished time periods (this week, so far, since 2020), and recent actions with present relevance/results. It is one of the hardest tenses for Turkish speakers because Turkish grammar does not distinguish 'finished specific past' from 'past with present relevance' the way English does.
topics.explanation_tr: Present perfect (have/has + past participle), geçmişi şimdiki zamana bağlar: belirli bir zamanı olmayan yaşam deneyimleri, bitmemiş zaman dilimleri (this week, so far, since 2020) ve şimdiki zamanla ilgisi/sonucu olan yakın geçmiş eylemler için kullanılır. Türkçe dilbilgisi 'belirli, bitmiş geçmiş' ile 'şimdiki zamanla ilgili geçmiş' arasında İngilizce'deki gibi bir ayrım yapmadığı için Türk öğrenciler için en zor zamanlardan biridir.
structure_patterns: S + have/has + V3 + since/for + time period
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'Since' bir başlangıç noktasını, 'for' bir süreyi gösterir; ikisi de present perfect'in en güvenilir sinyalleridir.

exceptions.rule: American English often accepts 'already/yet/just' with simple past too, but British/formal/academic English (closer to TOEFL norms) strongly prefers present perfect with these words.
exceptions.example: Have you finished yet? (preferred in formal/TOEFL contexts)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Amerikan İngilizcesinde 'already/yet/just' bazen simple past ile de kabul edilir, ancak British/resmi/akademik İngilizce (TOEFL normlarına daha yakın) bu kelimelerle present perfect'i tercih eder.

exceptions.rule: The past participle of irregular verbs must be memorized separately from the simple past form (go→went/gone, see→saw/seen).
exceptions.example: She has gone to the store. (NOT: has went)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Düzensiz fiillerin past participle hali, simple past halinden ayrı olarak ezberlenmelidir (go→went/gone, see→saw/seen).

examples.sentence: I have never been to Japan.
She has already finished her homework.
Have you ever taken the TOEFL before?
examples.translation: Daha önce hiç TOEFL sınavına girdin mi?

examples.sentence: We have lived in this city for ten years.
They haven't announced the results yet.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have seen him yesterday.
common_mistakes.correct: I saw him yesterday.
common_mistakes.explanation: Present perfect cannot be used with a specific finished-time expression like 'yesterday'; use simple past instead.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Present perfect, 'yesterday' gibi belirli bitmiş zaman ifadeleriyle kullanılmaz; simple past kullanılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: I am living here since 2015.
common_mistakes.correct: I have lived / have been living here since 2015.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Since' + a point in time requires present perfect (or perfect continuous), not present simple/continuous.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Since' + zaman noktası present perfect (ya da perfect continuous) gerektirir.

common_mistakes.wrong: She has went to the store.
common_mistakes.correct: She has gone to the store.
common_mistakes.explanation: The past participle of 'go' is 'gone', not 'went' (which is simple past).
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Go' fiilinin past participle hali 'gone'dur, 'went' değil (o simple past'tir).

common_mistakes.wrong: How long are you studying English?
common_mistakes.correct: How long have you been studying English?
common_mistakes.explanation: An ongoing situation that started in the past and continues now needs present perfect (continuous), not present simple/continuous alone.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Geçmişte başlayıp şu ana kadar süren bir durum için present perfect (continuous) gerekir, sadece present simple/continuous değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have finished my homework two hours ago.
common_mistakes.correct: I finished my homework two hours ago.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Ago' always refers to a specific, finished point in the past and therefore requires simple past, never present perfect.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Ago' her zaman belirli, bitmiş bir geçmiş zaman noktasına işaret eder; bu yüzden simple past gerektirir, present perfect asla kullanılmaz.

toefl_style_questions.question: Researchers ____ significant progress in the field of renewable energy over the past decade.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Over the past decade' bitmemiş bir zaman dilimidir, bu yüzden present perfect gerekir.

toefl_style_questions.question: This is the third time she ____ late for the meeting this month.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'This is the third time...' kalıbı, şu ana kadar tekrarlanan bir deneyimi anlatır, bu yüzden present perfect kullanılır: has been.

topics.toefl_tip: Present perfect vs. simple past confusion is one of the single most frequently tested grammar points on TOEFL for Turkish speakers, since Turkish has no direct grammatical equivalent.

topics.title: Future Forms (will, going to, present continuous)
topics.title_tr: Gelecek Zaman Biçimleri (will, going to, present continuous)
topics.explanation: English has no single dedicated future tense; instead, several forms express different shades of futurity: 'will' for predictions without present evidence, spontaneous decisions, and promises; 'going to' for pre-decided plans and predictions based on present evidence; present continuous for fixed arrangements; and present simple for scheduled/timetabled events (trains, classes). Choosing the right one depends entirely on context and speaker intention, not on a fixed rule.
topics.explanation_tr: İngilizce'de tek bir özel gelecek zaman yoktur; bunun yerine birkaç yapı farklı gelecek nüanslarını ifade eder: kanıta dayanmayan tahminler, ani kararlar ve sözler için 'will'; önceden verilmiş planlar ve kanıta dayalı tahminler için 'going to'; kesinleşmiş düzenlemeler için present continuous; ve programlanmış olaylar (tren, ders) için present simple. Doğru seçim tamamen bağlama ve konuşan kişinin niyetine bağlıdır, sabit bir kurala değil.
structure_patterns: S + am/is/are + going to + V(base) (plan/evidence-based prediction)
