topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'I think/probably' genellikle 'will' ile birlikte gelir; kesinleşmiş bir plan için 'going to' veya present continuous tercih edilir.

exceptions.rule: Time clauses (after, before, when, as soon as, until, if) referring to the future use present simple, not 'will', even though the meaning is future.
exceptions.example: I will call you when I arrive. (NOT: when I will arrive)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Gelecek zamana atıfta bulunan zaman cümlecikleri (after, before, when, as soon as, until, if) 'will' değil present simple kullanır, anlam gelecek olsa bile.

exceptions.rule: 'Shall' is an alternative to 'will' with I/we in formal British English, especially for suggestions and offers.
exceptions.example: Shall we start the meeting now?
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Shall', özellikle resmi İngiliz İngilizcesinde I/we ile 'will'e alternatif olarak, özellikle öneri ve teklif yaparken kullanılır.

examples.sentence: I think it will rain tomorrow.
We are going to launch the new product in March.
I'm meeting my accountant at 10 am tomorrow.
The train leaves at 6:15 every morning.
I promise I will call you as soon as I land.
examples.translation: İner inmez seni arayacağıma söz veriyorum.

common_mistakes.wrong: I will call you when I will arrive.
common_mistakes.correct: I will call you when I arrive.
common_mistakes.explanation: After time conjunctions like 'when', the future is expressed with present simple, not 'will', even though the overall sentence is about the future.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'When' gibi zaman bağlaçlarından sonra gelecek, 'will' ile değil present simple ile ifade edilir, cümlenin bütünü gelecekle ilgili olsa bile.

common_mistakes.wrong: Look at that car — it will crash!
common_mistakes.correct: Look at that car — it's going to crash!
common_mistakes.explanation: A prediction based on visible present evidence requires 'going to', not 'will', which is reserved for predictions without direct evidence.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Gözle görülür bir kanıta dayanan bir tahmin 'going to' gerektirir, doğrudan kanıt olmadan yapılan tahminlere ayrılan 'will' değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: I will meet my dentist tomorrow at 3; I arranged it last week.
common_mistakes.correct: I am meeting my dentist tomorrow at 3; I arranged it last week.
common_mistakes.explanation: A fixed, pre-arranged appointment is more naturally expressed with present continuous rather than 'will', which suggests the decision is being made now.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Önceden kesinleşmiş bir randevu, kararın şimdi verildiğini ima eden 'will' yerine present continuous ile daha doğal ifade edilir.

common_mistakes.wrong: The plane will depart at 9 am tomorrow according to the schedule, so we shall to be there by 8.
common_mistakes.correct: The plane departs at 9 am tomorrow according to the schedule, so we should be there by 8.
common_mistakes.explanation: A fixed timetable event uses present simple, and 'shall' (like all modals) is never followed by 'to'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Sabit bir tarife olayı present simple kullanır; 'shall' de (tüm modaller gibi) asla 'to' ile takip edilmez.

common_mistakes.wrong: I'm going to going to the party tonight.
common_mistakes.correct: I'm going to the party tonight.
common_mistakes.explanation: With the verb 'go' itself, the structure simplifies to 'going to + place', not the doubled 'going to go to'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Go' fiilinin kendisiyle yapı sadeleşir: 'going to + yer', çift 'going to go to' değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: As soon as the results ____ available, we will notify all applicants by email.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'As soon as' bir zaman bağlacıdır; gelecek anlamına rağmen 'will' değil present simple kullanılır.

toefl_style_questions.question: Judging by the dark sky and the wind picking up, a storm ____ hit the coast tonight.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Gözle görülür kanıta (kararan gökyüzü, artan rüzgar) dayanan bir tahmin için 'going to' kullanılır.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL frequently hides 'will' incorrectly placed after time conjunctions (when, after, as soon as, before, until, if) that require present simple in the future meaning.

topics.title: First Conditional
topics.explanation: The first conditional describes real, likely future situations and their probable results: 'If + present simple, ... will + base verb'. It expresses a genuine possibility the speaker believes could actually happen, unlike the second conditional, which is used for hypothetical or unlikely situations.
topics.explanation_tr: First conditional, gerçek ve muhtemel gelecek durumları ve olası sonuçlarını anlatır: 'If + present simple, ... will + yalın fiil'. Konuşmacının gerçekten gerçekleşebileceğine inandığı bir olasılığı ifade eder; varsayımsal veya olası olmayan durumlar için kullanılan second conditional'dan farklıdır.
structure_patterns: If + S + present simple, S + will + V(base)
S + will + V(base) + if + S + present simple
If + S + present simple, S + can/may/should + V(base)
Unless + S + present simple, S + will + V(base) (= if...not)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'Unless' = 'if...not' anlamına gelir ve if-clause'da olumsuz zaten var demektir, ekstra 'not' eklenmez.

exceptions.rule: The if-clause can also use present continuous or present perfect instead of present simple, depending on the meaning.
exceptions.example: If you have finished your work, you can leave early.
exceptions.explanation_tr: If-clause anlam gerektirdiğinde present simple yerine present continuous veya present perfect da kullanabilir.

exceptions.rule: The result clause can use modals other than 'will' (can, may, might, should) to express different degrees of certainty or advice.
exceptions.example: If it rains, we might cancel the trip.
exceptions.explanation_tr: Sonuç cümleciği farklı kesinlik veya öneri derecelerini ifade etmek için 'will' dışında modaller de (can, may, might, should) kullanabilir.

examples.sentence: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
You will pass the exam if you study hard.
Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.
If I finish work early, I might go to the gym.
examples.translation: İşi erken bitirirsem spor salonuna gidebilirim.

examples.sentence: As long as you follow the instructions, the machine will work properly.
examples.translation: Talimatları takip ettiğin sürece makine düzgün çalışacak.

common_mistakes.wrong: If it will rain, we will stay at home.
common_mistakes.correct: If it rains, we will stay at home.
common_mistakes.explanation: The if-clause of a first conditional never uses 'will'; it uses present simple, with 'will' reserved for the result clause only.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: First conditional'ın if-clause'unda asla 'will' kullanılmaz; if-clause present simple alır, 'will' sadece sonuç cümleciğinde kullanılır.

common_mistakes.wrong: If you don't hurry, you will not miss the bus.
common_mistakes.correct: If you don't hurry, you will miss the bus.
common_mistakes.explanation: This is a logical-meaning error rather than a grammar-form error: hurrying prevents missing the bus, so failing to hurry should lead to missing it, not the opposite.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Bu bir dilbilgisi biçimi hatası değil, mantık hatasıdır: acele etmek otobüsü kaçırmayı önler, bu yüzden acele etmemek otobüsü kaçırmaya yol açmalıdır, tersine değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: Unless you don't study, you will fail.
common_mistakes.correct: Unless you study, you will fail. / If you don't study, you will fail.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Unless' already means 'if...not', so adding another negative ('don't') after it creates an unintended double negative.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Unless' zaten 'if...not' anlamına gelir; sonrasına bir olumsuzluk daha ('don't') eklemek istenmeyen bir çift olumsuzluk yaratır.

common_mistakes.wrong: If she will study harder, she will get better grades.
common_mistakes.correct: If she studies harder, she will get better grades.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Will' must never appear in the if-clause of a real future conditional; only present simple is correct there.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Will', gerçek bir gelecek koşul cümlesinin if-clause'unda asla yer almamalıdır; orada sadece present simple doğrudur.

common_mistakes.wrong: If I will have free time, I will visit you.
common_mistakes.correct: If I have free time, I will visit you.
common_mistakes.explanation: Even when the meaning clearly refers to the future, the if-clause form remains present simple, not 'will have'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Anlam açıkça geleceğe atıfta bulunsa da, if-clause biçimi present simple olarak kalır, 'will have' değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: If the government ____ new regulations soon, air quality in the city will continue to decline.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: If-clause present simple gerektirir; 'will' kesinlikle if-clause'a girmez.

toefl_style_questions.question: You won't be allowed to enter the exam room ____ you arrive at least fifteen minutes early.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Unless' = 'if...not' anlamına gelir: girmene izin verilmeyecek, eğer erken gelmezsen demektir.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL almost always tests whether 'will' has been mistakenly placed in the if-clause of a real conditional, and checks the correct meaning of 'unless' as 'if...not'.

topics.title: Modals of Obligation and Advice (must, have to, should)
topics.title_tr: Zorunluluk ve Öneri Kipleri (must, have to, should)
topics.explanation: 'Must' and 'have to' both express obligation, but 'must' typically reflects the speaker's own authority or strong personal feeling, while 'have to' reflects an external rule or requirement. 'Should' expresses advice or a recommendation, weaker than obligation. Their negative forms differ sharply in meaning: 'mustn't' means prohibition, while 'don't have to' means the action is optional, not forbidden.
topics.explanation_tr: 'Must' ve 'have to' ikisi de zorunluluk ifade eder, ancak 'must' genellikle konuşmacının kendi yetkisini veya güçlü kişisel görüşünü yansıtır; 'have to' ise dışarıdan gelen bir kural veya gerekliliği yansıtır. 'Should' ise zorunluluktan daha zayıf bir öneri veya tavsiye ifade eder. Olumsuz biçimleri anlam olarak keskin biçimde ayrışır: 'mustn't' yasaklama anlamına gelirken, 'don't have to' eylemin isteğe bağlı olduğunu, yasak olmadığını belirtir.
structure_patterns: S + don't/doesn't have to + V(base) (no obligation, optional)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'Mustn't' ve 'don't have to' zıt anlamlar taşır; bu ikisi TOEFL'da en sık karıştırılan çift arasındadır.

exceptions.rule: 'Have to' (not 'must') is used to form questions and past forms, since 'must' has no past tense of its own.
exceptions.example: Did you have to wait long? / I had to leave early yesterday.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Must'ın kendi geçmiş zaman biçimi olmadığı için soru ve geçmiş zaman kurarken 'have to' kullanılır.

exceptions.rule: 'Must' can also express strong logical certainty/deduction, not just obligation.
exceptions.example: She hasn't answered her phone all day; she must be very busy.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Must' sadece zorunluluk değil, güçlü mantıksal kesinlik/çıkarım da ifade edebilir.

examples.sentence: You must wear a seatbelt in this country.
examples.translation: Bu ülkede emniyet kemeri takmak zorundasın.

examples.sentence: I have to finish this report by Friday.
examples.translation: Bu raporu Cuma'ya kadar bitirmem gerekiyor.

examples.sentence: You mustn't smoke inside the building.
You don't have to come if you're busy.
You should see a doctor about that cough.
examples.translation: O öksürük için bir doktora görünmelisin.

common_mistakes.wrong: You mustn't worry if you can't finish today; you can do it tomorrow.
common_mistakes.correct: You don't have to worry if you can't finish today; you can do it tomorrow.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Mustn't' wrongly implies prohibition (forbidden to worry), while the intended meaning is that worrying is simply unnecessary, which requires 'don't have to'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Mustn't' burada yanlışlıkla yasak anlamı taşır (endişelenmek yasak); asıl anlam endişelenmenin gerekli olmadığıdır, bu da 'don't have to' gerektirir.

common_mistakes.wrong: I must to finish this today.
common_mistakes.correct: I must finish this today.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Must', like all modal verbs, is directly followed by the base verb with no 'to'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Must', diğer tüm modal fiiller gibi, doğrudan yalın fiille takip edilir, araya 'to' girmez.

common_mistakes.wrong: Did you must wait a long time?
common_mistakes.correct: Did you have to wait a long time?
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Must' cannot form questions with 'did'; 'have to' must be used instead in past questions.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Must' 'did' ile soru kuramaz; geçmiş zaman sorularında 'have to' kullanılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: You should to see a doctor.
common_mistakes.correct: You should see a doctor.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Should', as a modal verb, is never followed by 'to' before the main verb.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Should' bir modal fiil olarak asla ana fiilden önce 'to' ile takip edilmez.

common_mistakes.wrong: He musted finish the project last week.
common_mistakes.correct: He had to finish the project last week.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Must' has no past tense form ('musted' does not exist); 'had to' is the correct past equivalent.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Must'ın geçmiş zaman biçimi yoktur ('musted' diye bir şey yoktur); doğru geçmiş zaman karşılığı 'had to'dur.

toefl_style_questions.question: Employees ____ wear identification badges at all times while inside the building, according to company policy.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Must' doğrudan yalın fiille kullanılır; 'to' eklenmez.

toefl_style_questions.question: You ____ bring your own laptop to the workshop; the organizers will provide one for every participant.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Organizatörler zaten laptop sağlayacağı için katılımcı laptop getirmek zorunda değildir (yasak değil, isteğe bağlı): don't have to.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL frequently tests the contrast between 'mustn't' (prohibition) and 'don't have to' (no obligation), as well as the impossible modal + 'to' pattern.

topics.title: Relative Clauses (Defining) — who, which, that, where
topics.title_tr: İlgi Cümlecikleri (Tanımlayan) — who, which, that, where
topics.explanation: Defining relative clauses give essential information that identifies exactly which person or thing is being talked about, and cannot be removed without changing the meaning. 'Who/that' refer to people, 'which/that' refer to things, and 'where' refers to places. No comma is used before a defining relative clause.
topics.explanation_tr: Tanımlayan ilgi cümlecikleri, kimden veya neden bahsedildiğini tam olarak belirleyen temel bilgiyi verir ve cümleden çıkarılırsa anlam değişir. 'Who/that' insanlara, 'which/that' nesnelere, 'where' ise yerlere atıfta bulunur. Tanımlayan ilgi cümleciğinden önce virgül kullanılmaz.
structure_patterns: noun (person, object of clause) + who/whom/that/(nothing) + S + V
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'That' hem insan hem nesne için tanımlayan cümleciklerde kullanılabilir, ancak tanımlamayan (virgüllü) cümleciklerde kullanılamaz.

exceptions.rule: The relative pronoun can be omitted when it is the object of the relative clause (not the subject).
exceptions.example: The book (that) I read last week was excellent.
exceptions.explanation_tr: İlgi zamiri, ilgi cümleciğinin öznesi değil nesnesi olduğunda cümleden çıkarılabilir.

exceptions.rule: 'Whose' shows possession and is used for both people and things, replacing a possessive adjective.
exceptions.example: That's the man whose car was stolen.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Whose' sahiplik gösterir ve hem insanlar hem nesneler için, bir iyelik sıfatının yerine kullanılır.

examples.sentence: The woman who called you is my sister.
examples.translation: Seni arayan kadın benim kız kardeşim.

examples.sentence: This is the book that I told you about.
The restaurant where we ate last night was excellent.
examples.translation: Dün gece yemek yediğimiz restoran mükemmeldi.

examples.sentence: I have a friend whose father is a famous painter.
examples.translation: Babası ünlü bir ressam olan bir arkadaşım var.

examples.sentence: The laptop which I bought last month stopped working.
examples.translation: Geçen ay aldığım dizüstü bilgisayar çalışmayı kesti.

common_mistakes.wrong: The man which called you is my uncle.
common_mistakes.correct: The man who called you is my uncle.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Which' cannot refer to a person; 'who' or 'that' must be used for people, and this substitution is a very common learner error.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Which' bir insana atıfta bulunamaz; insanlar için 'who' veya 'that' kullanılmalıdır; bu değişim çok yaygın bir öğrenci hatasıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: This is the book who I bought yesterday.
common_mistakes.correct: This is the book that/which I bought yesterday.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Who' cannot refer to a thing; 'that' or 'which' must be used for objects.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Who' bir nesneye atıfta bulunamaz; nesneler için 'that' veya 'which' kullanılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: The city where I was born there is very small.
common_mistakes.correct: The city where I was born is very small.
common_mistakes.explanation: Adding an extra pronoun ('there') after the relative clause duplicates the meaning already carried by 'where' and must be removed.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: İlgi cümleciğinden sonra ekstra bir zamir ('there') eklemek, 'where' tarafından zaten taşınan anlamı tekrarlar ve kaldırılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: The teacher, that taught me English, was very kind.
common_mistakes.correct: The teacher who taught me English was very kind.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'That' should not be preceded by a comma in a defining clause, and here the comma incorrectly suggests a non-defining clause where 'that' would not even be allowed; also 'who', not 'that', is the more standard choice with a comma-free defining clause about a person.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'That'ten önce tanımlayan cümlecikte virgül kullanılmaz; buradaki virgül yanlışlıkla tanımlamayan bir cümlecik önerir ki orada 'that' bile kullanılamaz; ayrıca insanlar için virgülsüz tanımlayan cümlecikte daha standart seçim 'who'dur.

common_mistakes.wrong: The girl her bag was stolen is crying.
common_mistakes.correct: The girl whose bag was stolen is crying.
common_mistakes.explanation: A possessive relative pronoun 'whose' is required to link the possession to the noun; a plain possessive adjective ('her') cannot function as a relative pronoun.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Sahiplik ilişkisini isme bağlamak için iyelik ilgi zamiri 'whose' gereklidir; sıradan bir iyelik sıfatı ('her') ilgi zamiri olarak görev yapamaz.

toefl_style_questions.question: The scientist ____ research led to this discovery received an award last month.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Bilim insanının araştırmasına (sahiplik ilişkisi) atıfta bulunulduğu için 'whose' gereklidir.

toefl_style_questions.question: The museum ____ we visited last summer has just opened a new exhibit.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Museum' bir nesne/yer olarak burada doğrudan nesnesi olduğu için 'which' (veya 'that') kullanılır; 'where' zarf işlevi görür ve burada cümle yapısına uymaz çünkü fiilin nesnesi gerekir.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL commonly swaps who/which/where to test whether the student can distinguish between people, things, and places, and tests the missing/extra pronoun after relative clauses.

topics.title: Gerunds and Infinitives (Basic Patterns)
topics.explanation: Some verbs are followed by a gerund (V-ing), some by a to-infinitive (to + V), and some by either with a change in meaning. There is no logical rule for which pattern a verb takes — it depends on the specific verb and must be learned through exposure and memorization of common verb groups.
topics.explanation_tr: Bazı fiiller gerund (V-ing) alır, bazıları to-infinitive (to + V) alır, bazıları ise ikisini de alabilir ve anlam değişir. Hangi fiilin hangi kalıbı aldığına dair mantıksal bir kural yoktur; bu, yaygın fiil gruplarının maruz kalma ve ezber yoluyla öğrenilmesine bağlıdır.
structure_patterns: verb + object + to V (want someone to do something)
stop/remember/forget + V-ing vs. + to V (meaning changes)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Her fiil grubunun kendine özgü kalıbı vardır; bu yüzden bu fiiller ayrı ayrı listeler halinde ezberlenmelidir.

exceptions.rule: 'Stop', 'remember', and 'forget' change meaning depending on whether they are followed by -ing or to-infinitive.
exceptions.example: I stopped smoking (quit the habit). / I stopped to smoke (paused another activity in order to smoke).
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Stop', 'remember' ve 'forget' -ing veya to-infinitive alıp almadığına göre anlam değiştirir.

exceptions.rule: After a preposition, a verb almost always takes the -ing form, never the to-infinitive.
exceptions.example: She is interested in learning Spanish. (NOT: in to learn)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Bir edattan sonra fiil neredeyse her zaman -ing formunu alır, asla to-infinitive almaz.

examples.sentence: I enjoy reading novels in my free time.
examples.translation: Boş zamanımda roman okumaktan zevk alırım.

examples.sentence: She decided to change her career.
They suggested waiting until next week.
He is looking forward to meeting you.
We hope to finish the project on time.

common_mistakes.wrong: I enjoy to read novels.
common_mistakes.correct: I enjoy reading novels.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Enjoy' must be followed by the gerund (-ing), never by a to-infinitive, unlike verbs such as 'want' or 'decide'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Enjoy' fiilinden sonra her zaman gerund (-ing) gelir, 'want' veya 'decide' gibi fiillerin aksine to-infinitive gelmez.

common_mistakes.wrong: She decided going to the party.
common_mistakes.correct: She decided to go to the party.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Decide' is followed by a to-infinitive, not a gerund.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Decide' fiilinden sonra to-infinitive gelir, gerund değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: I am interested to learn French.
common_mistakes.correct: I am interested in learning French.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Interested' is followed by the preposition 'in', and after a preposition, only the -ing form is possible, not a to-infinitive.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Interested'ten sonra edat 'in' gelir; bir edattan sonra sadece -ing formu mümkündür, to-infinitive değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: He stopped to smoke five years ago (meaning: he quit smoking).
common_mistakes.correct: He stopped smoking five years ago.
common_mistakes.explanation: To express quitting a habit, 'stop' must be followed by -ing; 'stop to + verb' instead means pausing another action in order to do something.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Bir alışkanlığı bırakmayı ifade etmek için 'stop'tan sonra -ing gelmelidir; 'stop to + fiil' ise başka bir eylemi durdurup bir şey yapmak için ara vermek anlamına gelir.

common_mistakes.wrong: They suggested to wait until next week.
common_mistakes.correct: They suggested waiting until next week.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund (or a that-clause), never directly by a to-infinitive.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Suggest' fiilinden sonra gerund (veya 'that' cümleciği) gelir, doğrudan to-infinitive asla gelmez.

toefl_style_questions.question: The committee is considering ____ the deadline for submissions by two weeks.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Consider' fiilinden sonra gerund (-ing) gelir, to-infinitive değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: After finishing the report, she remembered ____ the attachment before sending the email.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Burada 'remember' bir görevi yapmayı hatırlama anlamındadır (unutmadan yapma); bu anlam için to-infinitive kullanılır.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests specific verb + gerund/infinitive collocations (enjoy doing, decide to do, suggest doing) and the meaning shift with stop/remember/forget + -ing vs. to-infinitive.

topics.title: Present Perfect Continuous
topics.explanation: Present perfect continuous (have/has + been + V-ing) emphasizes the duration or ongoing nature of an activity that started in the past and either continues now or has just stopped, often with visible present results. It overlaps with present perfect simple, but continuous form stresses the process/duration, while simple present perfect stresses the completed result or number of times.
topics.explanation_tr: Present perfect continuous (have/has + been + V-ing), geçmişte başlayıp şu ana kadar süren veya az önce biten, genellikle görünür şimdiki sonuçları olan bir eylemin süresini veya devamlılığını vurgular. Present perfect simple ile örtüşür, ancak continuous form süreci/süreyi vurgularken, simple present perfect tamamlanmış sonucu veya kaç kez yapıldığını vurgular.
structure_patterns: S + have/has + been + V-ing + for/since + time
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'How long' sorusu genellikle present perfect continuous ile cevaplanır, özellikle eylem hâlâ sürüyorsa.

exceptions.rule: Stative verbs cannot be used in continuous forms, so present perfect simple must be used instead, even with 'for/since'.
exceptions.example: I have known her for ten years. (NOT: have been knowing)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Durum fiilleri continuous formda kullanılamaz; bu yüzden 'for/since' ile bile present perfect simple kullanılmalıdır.

exceptions.rule: When emphasizing quantity/number of completed actions rather than duration, present perfect simple is preferred over continuous.
exceptions.example: I have written three emails this morning. (not: have been writing, if the focus is the completed count)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Süre değil, tamamlanan eylem sayısı/miktarı vurgulanıyorsa continuous yerine present perfect simple tercih edilir.

examples.sentence: I have been studying English for three years.
She has been working on this project since Monday.
examples.translation: Pazartesi'den beri bu proje üzerinde çalışıyor.

examples.sentence: It has been raining all day.
Have you been waiting long?
They have been arguing about the budget for hours.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have been knowing him since university.
common_mistakes.correct: I have known him since university.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and cannot take the continuous form, even in the present perfect continuous.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Know' bir durum fiilidir ve present perfect continuous'ta bile continuous form alamaz.

common_mistakes.wrong: She is working here since 2018.
common_mistakes.correct: She has been working here since 2018.
common_mistakes.explanation: A situation continuing from the past to now with 'since' requires present perfect (continuous), not present continuous alone.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Since' ile geçmişten şu ana süregelen bir durum present perfect (continuous) gerektirir, tek başına present continuous değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: How long have you been study English?
common_mistakes.correct: How long have you been studying English?
common_mistakes.explanation: After 'have/has been', the main verb must take the -ing ending; the base form alone is incorrect here.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Have/has been'den sonra ana fiil -ing eki almalıdır; burada yalın form yanlıştır.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have been eating this cake since two hours.
common_mistakes.correct: I have been eating this cake for two hours.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'For' is used with a duration/length of time (two hours), while 'since' is used with a starting point (2 pm, Monday); confusing these two is extremely common.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'For' bir süre/uzunluk (two hours) ile kullanılır, 'since' ise bir başlangıç noktası (2 pm, Monday) ile kullanılır; bu ikisini karıştırmak çok yaygındır.

common_mistakes.wrong: They have been argue about the budget for hours.
common_mistakes.correct: They have been arguing about the budget for hours.
common_mistakes.explanation: The base form cannot follow 'have been'; the -ing form is obligatory to form the continuous aspect.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Have been'den sonra yalın form gelemez; continuous yapıyı oluşturmak için -ing formu zorunludur.

toefl_style_questions.question: The negotiators ____ for over six hours, but they still haven't reached an agreement.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'For over six hours' süreyi vurgular ve eylem hâlâ sonuçsuz sürmektedir, bu yüzden present perfect continuous uygundur.

toefl_style_questions.question: I ____ this author's novels since I was a teenager; I must have read almost all of them.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Since I was a teenager' başlangıç noktasını gösterir ve süregelen bir alışkanlık/süreci vurgular, bu yüzden present perfect continuous kullanılır.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests the for/since distinction heavily, and checks whether stative verbs have been mistakenly placed into the continuous perfect form.

topics.title: Question Tags
topics.explanation: Question tags are short questions (isn't it?, don't you?, will she?) added to the end of a statement to confirm information or invite agreement. The rule is strict and mechanical: a positive statement takes a negative tag, and a negative statement takes a positive tag, using the same auxiliary/modal verb (or a form of 'do' if the main verb has no auxiliary) and matching the subject with a pronoun.
topics.explanation_tr: Soru ekleri (isn't it?, don't you?, will she?), bir ifadeye bilgiyi doğrulamak veya onay almak amacıyla eklenen kısa sorulardır. Kural kesin ve mekaniktir: olumlu bir ifade olumsuz bir ek alır, olumsuz bir ifade olumlu bir ek alır; aynı yardımcı/modal fiil (ana fiilin yardımcı fiili yoksa 'do'nun bir biçimi) kullanılır ve özne bir zamirle eşleştirilir.
structure_patterns: Positive statement + negative tag (auxiliary + n't + subject pronoun)
Negative statement + positive tag (auxiliary + subject pronoun)
Statement with 'to be'/modal → tag repeats 'to be'/modal
Statement with plain verb → tag uses do/does/did
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Ek her zaman ana cümledeki yardımcı fiile ve özneye göre şekillenir; ana fiile göre değil.

exceptions.rule: 'I am' takes the irregular tag 'aren't I?', not 'am I not?' in normal spoken usage (though 'am I not' is possible in very formal style).
exceptions.example: I'm right, aren't I?
exceptions.explanation_tr: Konuşmada 'I am' genellikle düzensiz ek 'aren't I?' alır, 'am I not?' değil (çok resmi üslupta bu da mümkündür).

exceptions.rule: After 'Let's', the tag is always 'shall we?', regardless of the rest of the sentence.
exceptions.example: Let's go to the cinema, shall we?
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Let's'ten sonra ek her zaman 'shall we?' olur, cümlenin başka bir kısmına bakılmaksızın.

exceptions.rule: After a sentence with 'nothing/nobody/no one' as subject (negative meaning), the tag is positive, using 'they' for people.
exceptions.example: Nobody called, did they?
exceptions.explanation_tr: Öznesi 'nothing/nobody/no one' olan (olumsuz anlam taşıyan) bir cümlede ek olumlu olur; insanlar için 'they' kullanılır.

examples.sentence: You live in Istanbul, don't you?
She isn't coming tonight, is she?
examples.translation: O bu akşam gelmiyor, değil mi?

examples.sentence: They have finished the project, haven't they?
He can speak French, can't he?
Let's take a break, shall we?

common_mistakes.wrong: You live in Istanbul, do you?
common_mistakes.correct: You live in Istanbul, don't you?
common_mistakes.explanation: A positive statement must take a negative tag; a positive tag on a positive statement is grammatically inconsistent (and would sound like genuine surprise, not confirmation).
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Olumlu bir ifade olumsuz bir ek almalıdır; olumlu ifadeye olumlu ek eklemek dilbilgisel olarak tutarsızdır (ve onay değil, gerçek bir şaşkınlık anlamı verir).

common_mistakes.wrong: She can't drive, can she not?
common_mistakes.correct: She can't drive, can she?
common_mistakes.explanation: Negative statements take a simple positive tag; there is no need (and it is incorrect) to add 'not' again in the tag.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Olumsuz ifadeler sadece olumlu bir ek alır; ekte tekrar 'not' eklemeye gerek yoktur (ve bu yanlıştır).

common_mistakes.wrong: You like pizza, isn't it?
common_mistakes.correct: You like pizza, don't you?
common_mistakes.explanation: The tag must match the main verb's auxiliary; since there is no 'to be' in the main clause, 'do/don't' must be used, not 'isn't it', which learners often use as a frozen, universal tag.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Ek, ana fiilin yardımcı fiiline uymalıdır; ana cümlede 'to be' olmadığı için 'do/don't' kullanılmalıdır, öğrencilerin genellikle evrensel bir ek gibi kullandığı 'isn't it' değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: He has a car, hasn't he has?
common_mistakes.correct: He has a car, hasn't he?
common_mistakes.explanation: The tag should not repeat the main verb again after the pronoun; it consists only of auxiliary + n't (or not) + subject pronoun.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Ek, zamirden sonra ana fiili tekrar etmemelidir; sadece yardımcı fiil + n't (veya not) + özne zamirinden oluşur.

common_mistakes.wrong: Nobody called, didn't they?
common_mistakes.correct: Nobody called, did they?
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Nobody' already carries a negative meaning, so the statement is treated as negative and needs a positive tag, not a negative one.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Nobody' zaten olumsuz bir anlam taşır, bu yüzden ifade olumsuz kabul edilir ve olumlu bir ek gerekir, olumsuz değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: You haven't submitted the application yet, ____?
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Ana cümle olumsuz olduğu için (haven't), ek olumlu olur: have you.

toefl_style_questions.question: Let's review the contract one more time before signing, ____?
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Let's' ile başlayan cümlelerde ek her zaman 'shall we?' olur.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests whether the tag correctly mirrors the auxiliary of the main clause and flips positive/negative correctly, especially in negative-subject sentences (nobody, nothing).

topics.title: Past Perfect
topics.explanation: Past perfect (had + past participle) describes an action that was completed before another point or action in the past. It establishes a clear sequence: the past perfect action happened first, and the simple past action happened second. Without past perfect, the order of two past events can become ambiguous or simply wrong.
topics.explanation_tr: Past perfect (had + past participle), geçmişte başka bir zaman noktasından veya eylemden önce tamamlanmış bir eylemi anlatır. Açık bir sıralama kurar: past perfect eylemi önce, simple past eylemi sonra gerçekleşmiştir. Past perfect olmadan, iki geçmiş olayın sırası belirsiz ya da tamamen yanlış olabilir.
structure_patterns: By the time + S + V-ed, S + had + V3
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'By the time' genellikle past perfect'in en güçlü sinyalidir; iki geçmiş olay arasındaki önce-sonra ilişkisini kurar.

exceptions.rule: When the order of events is already clear from 'before' or 'after', past simple can sometimes be used for both clauses in informal speech, though past perfect remains more precise and is preferred in formal/academic writing.
exceptions.example: After she finished her homework, she watched TV. (informal, order is clear from 'after')
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Before/after' ile olay sırası zaten belirginse, gündelik konuşmada her iki cümlecik için simple past kullanılabilir; ancak resmi/akademik yazıda past perfect daha kesin ve tercih edilen seçenektir.

examples.sentence: By the time we arrived, the movie had already started.
She had never seen snow before she moved to Canada.
examples.translation: Kanada'ya taşınmadan önce hiç kar görmemişti.

examples.sentence: I had finished my homework before dinner.
Had you met him before the conference?
The train had left before we got to the station.

common_mistakes.wrong: When I arrived, the meeting already finished.
common_mistakes.correct: When I arrived, the meeting had already finished.
common_mistakes.explanation: To show that one past event (the meeting finishing) happened before another (arriving), past perfect must be used, not simple past.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Bir geçmiş olayın (toplantının bitmesi) diğerinden (varmak) önce gerçekleştiğini göstermek için past perfect kullanılmalıdır, simple past değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: She had went to bed before I called.
common_mistakes.correct: She had gone to bed before I called.
common_mistakes.explanation: Past perfect uses the past participle (gone), not the simple past form (went), after 'had'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Past perfect, 'had'den sonra past participle (gone) kullanır, simple past biçimi (went) değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: I had finished my homework, then I watched TV.
common_mistakes.correct: I had finished my homework before I watched TV. / I finished my homework, and then I watched TV.
common_mistakes.explanation: Past perfect should be paired with a clear reference point (before/when/by the time); using it loosely with 'then' without that reference point sounds unnatural, and simple past is often more natural for a simple sequence of completed actions.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Past perfect, açık bir referans noktasıyla (before/when/by the time) eşleştirilmelidir; bu referans noktası olmadan 'then' ile gevşek kullanmak doğal değildir; basit bir tamamlanmış olaylar dizisi için genellikle simple past daha doğaldır.

common_mistakes.wrong: By the time she called, I have left the office.
common_mistakes.correct: By the time she called, I had left the office.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'By the time' + past simple in one clause requires past perfect in the other clause to show the earlier event, not present perfect.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'By the time' + past simple bir cümlecikte kullanıldığında, daha önceki olayı göstermek için diğer cümlecikte past perfect gerekir, present perfect değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: He had never seen snow, then he moves to Canada.
common_mistakes.correct: He had never seen snow before he moved to Canada.
common_mistakes.explanation: The second clause must be in simple past to mark the specific past event, and a proper time conjunction ('before') should connect the two clauses.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: İkinci cümlecik, belirli geçmiş olayı işaretlemek için simple past'te olmalıdır ve iki cümleciği bağlamak için uygun bir zaman bağlacı ('before') kullanılmalıdır.

toefl_style_questions.question: By the time the fire department arrived, the flames ____ most of the building.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: İtfaiye varmadan önce yangının çoğunu yok ettiği belirtildiği için past perfect kullanılır.

toefl_style_questions.question: She realized that she ____ her passport at home only after she reached the airport.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Pasaportu evde bırakma eylemi, havaalanına ulaşmadan önce gerçekleşmiştir, bu yüzden past perfect kullanılır.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests past perfect heavily in sentences with 'by the time', 'before', 'after', and 'already' where two past events must be placed in the correct order.

topics.title: Second Conditional
topics.explanation: The second conditional expresses hypothetical, unreal, or unlikely situations in the present or future, and their imagined results: 'If + past simple, ... would + base verb'. Despite using a past-tense form in the if-clause, it does not refer to real past time — this shift to past tense is purely grammatical, marking unreality, which is a major source of confusion for learners.
topics.explanation_tr: Second conditional, şimdiki veya gelecekteki varsayımsal, gerçek olmayan veya olası olmayan durumları ve bunların hayali sonuçlarını ifade eder: 'If + past simple, ... would + yalın fiil'. If-clause'ta geçmiş zaman biçimi kullanılsa da bu gerçek bir geçmiş zamana atıfta bulunmaz — bu geçmiş zamana kayış tamamen dilbilgisel olup gerçek-dışılığı işaretler; bu, öğrenciler için büyük bir kafa karışıklığı kaynağıdır.
structure_patterns: If + S + past simple, S + would + V(base)
S + would + V(base) + if + S + past simple
If I were you, I would + V(base)
If + S + past simple, S + could/might + V(base)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'If I were you' kalıbı, gerçek dışı öneri verirken kullanılan sabit bir kalıptır ve 'was' değil 'were' kullanılır (formal İngilizce'de).

exceptions.rule: In the if-clause, formal English uses 'were' for all subjects (I, he, she, it) instead of 'was', especially in the fixed expression 'If I were you'.
exceptions.example: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
exceptions.explanation_tr: Resmi İngilizce'de if-clause'da tüm özneler için (I, he, she, it) 'was' yerine 'were' kullanılır, özellikle sabit ifade 'If I were you'da.

exceptions.rule: 'Could' and 'might' can replace 'would' in the result clause to express ability or a weaker possibility rather than a direct hypothetical result.
exceptions.example: If I had more time, I could learn another language.
exceptions.explanation_tr: Sonuç cümleciğinde 'would' yerine 'could' veya 'might' kullanılabilir; bu, doğrudan varsayımsal bir sonuç yerine yetenek veya daha zayıf bir olasılık ifade eder.

examples.sentence: If I had more money, I would travel around the world.
examples.translation: Daha fazla param olsaydı, dünyayı gezerdim.

examples.sentence: If she knew the truth, she would be very upset.
If I were you, I wouldn't sign that contract.
examples.translation: Senin yerinde olsam, o sözleşmeyi imzalamazdım.

examples.sentence: What would you do if you won the lottery?
If we lived closer to the city, we could walk to work.
examples.translation: Şehre daha yakın yaşasaydık, işe yürüyerek gidebilirdik.

common_mistakes.wrong: If I would have more money, I would travel.
common_mistakes.correct: If I had more money, I would travel.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Would' must never appear in the if-clause of a second conditional; only past simple is correct there, with 'would' reserved for the result clause.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Would', second conditional'ın if-clause'unda asla yer almamalıdır; orada sadece past simple doğrudur, 'would' sonuç cümleciğine ayrılmıştır.

common_mistakes.wrong: If I was you, I would accept the offer.
common_mistakes.correct: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
common_mistakes.explanation: In the fixed and formal expression 'if I were you', 'were' is required even though 'I' would normally take 'was' in ordinary past tense.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Sabit ve resmi ifade 'if I were you'da 'were' gereklidir, normal geçmiş zamanda 'I' genellikle 'was' alsa bile.

common_mistakes.wrong: If she has more free time, she would learn painting.
common_mistakes.correct: If she had more free time, she would learn painting.
common_mistakes.explanation: The if-clause of a second (hypothetical) conditional needs past simple, not present simple, which is reserved for the first (real) conditional.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Second (varsayımsal) conditional'ın if-clause'u past simple gerektirir, present simple değil; present simple first (gerçek) conditional'a ayrılmıştır.

common_mistakes.wrong: I would travel if I will have more money.
common_mistakes.correct: I would travel if I had more money.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Will' cannot appear in the if-clause of any conditional using 'would' in the result clause; only past simple belongs there for hypothetical meaning.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Will', sonuç cümleciğinde 'would' kullanan hiçbir koşul cümlesinin if-clause'unda yer alamaz; varsayımsal anlam için orada sadece past simple bulunur.

common_mistakes.wrong: If I were rich, I will buy a big house.
common_mistakes.correct: If I were rich, I would buy a big house.
common_mistakes.explanation: Once the if-clause signals a hypothetical/unreal situation with past simple ('were'), the result clause must use 'would', not 'will'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: If-clause past simple ('were') ile varsayımsal/gerçek dışı bir durumu işaretlediğinde, sonuç cümleciği 'would' kullanmalıdır, 'will' değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: If the company ____ its marketing strategy, it would likely attract a younger audience.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Sonuç cümleciğinde 'would' olduğu için if-clause past simple ('changed') gerektirir.

toefl_style_questions.question: If I ____ in your position, I would think twice before making such a risky investment.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Formal İngilizce'de 'if I were' kalıbı tercih edilir, özellikle tavsiye verirken.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests whether 'would' or 'will' has been incorrectly placed in the if-clause of a hypothetical conditional, and checks the formal use of 'were' instead of 'was' with I/he/she/it.

topics.title: Passive Voice
topics.explanation: The passive voice (be + past participle) shifts focus from the doer of an action to the receiver of the action, and is used when the agent is unknown, unimportant, or obvious from context — very common in academic and formal writing, including TOEFL reading passages. The tense of the sentence is carried entirely by the form of 'be'; the main verb always stays as the past participle.
topics.explanation_tr: Edilgen çatı (be + past participle), odağı eylemi yapan kişiden eylemi alan kişiye/nesneye kaydırır ve eylemi yapan bilinmiyorsa, önemsizse veya bağlamdan açıkça anlaşılıyorsa kullanılır — akademik ve resmi yazıda, TOEFL okuma metinleri dahil, çok yaygındır. Cümlenin zamanı tamamen 'be' fiilinin biçimiyle taşınır; ana fiil her zaman past participle olarak kalır.
structure_patterns: S(receiver) + will be/can be/should be + V3
S(receiver) + be + V3 + by + agent (when the doer matters)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'By' agent'ı (eylemi yapanı) tanıtır, ancak birçok pasif cümlede agent hiç belirtilmez.

exceptions.rule: Intransitive verbs (verbs with no object, like 'happen', 'arrive', 'sleep') cannot be made passive, because passive requires an object to become the new subject.
exceptions.example: The accident happened yesterday. (NOT: was happened)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Geçişsiz fiiller (nesnesi olmayan fiiller, örn. 'happen', 'arrive', 'sleep') pasif yapılamaz, çünkü pasif için yeni özne olacak bir nesne gerekir.

exceptions.rule: The tense of the active sentence is preserved by changing the form of 'be'; the past participle itself never changes to show tense.
exceptions.example: Active: The company built the factory in 1990. → Passive: The factory was built in 1990.
exceptions.explanation_tr: Aktif cümlenin zamanı, 'be' fiilinin biçimi değiştirilerek korunur; past participle'ın kendisi zamanı göstermek için asla değişmez.

examples.sentence: The bridge was built in 1932.
This report has been reviewed by three experts.
examples.translation: Bu rapor üç uzman tarafından incelendi.

examples.sentence: New regulations are being introduced next month.
The problem will be solved by our technical team.
English is spoken in many countries around the world.
examples.translation: İngilizce dünya çapında birçok ülkede konuşulur.

common_mistakes.wrong: The letter was write by my brother.
common_mistakes.correct: The letter was written by my brother.
common_mistakes.explanation: In the passive voice, the main verb must be in the past participle form (written), not the base form (write).
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Edilgen çatıda ana fiil past participle biçiminde olmalıdır (written), yalın biçimde değil (write).

common_mistakes.wrong: The accident was happened near my house.
common_mistakes.correct: The accident happened near my house.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Happen' is intransitive and cannot be passive; it should be used in the active form for both meaning and grammar to be correct.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Happen' geçişsizdir ve pasif yapılamaz; hem anlam hem dilbilgisi açısından aktif biçimde kullanılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: This book is reading by millions of people.
common_mistakes.correct: This book is read by millions of people.
common_mistakes.explanation: The passive requires the past participle (read), not the -ing form, which would incorrectly create a continuous active-sounding structure.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Pasif çatı past participle gerektirir (read), -ing formu değil; -ing formu yanlışlıkla continuous/aktif görünümlü bir yapı oluşturur.

common_mistakes.wrong: The new policy is decided by the board next week.
common_mistakes.correct: The new policy will be decided by the board next week.
common_mistakes.explanation: A future event needs the future passive form ('will be + V3'); using present passive here incorrectly implies the decision is already habitual or currently occurring.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Gelecekte gerçekleşecek bir olay için gelecek zaman pasif biçimi ('will be + V3') gerekir; burada present passive kullanmak yanlışlıkla kararın zaten alışılmış veya şu anda gerçekleştiğini ima eder.

common_mistakes.wrong: She was gave an award for her research.
common_mistakes.correct: She was given an award for her research.
common_mistakes.explanation: The irregular past participle of 'give' is 'given', not 'gave' (which is the simple past form used only in active sentences).
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Give' fiilinin düzensiz past participle hali 'given'dır, sadece aktif cümlelerde kullanılan simple past biçimi 'gave' değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: Every year, thousands of new species ____ by scientists around the world.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Odak keşfedilen türlerdedir, keşfeden bilim insanları değil, bu yüzden pasif çatı kullanılır.

toefl_style_questions.question: The final decision ____ by the board of directors by the end of this week.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Odak, kararı alanlar değil kararın kendisidir ve gelecek zamanda gerçekleşecektir, bu yüzden 'will be made' gerekir.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests whether the past participle form is correctly used after 'be' (not the base or -ing form), and checks whether an intransitive verb has been incorrectly made passive.

topics.title: Reported (Indirect) Speech
topics.explanation: Reported speech conveys what someone said without quoting their exact words. When the reporting verb is in the past (said, told, asked), the tense in the reported clause typically shifts one step back (present→past, past→past perfect, will→would), and pronouns/time expressions adjust to fit the new speaker/time perspective (I→he/she, tomorrow→the next day).
topics.explanation_tr: Aktarılan anlatım, birinin söylediklerini tam kelimeleriyle alıntılamadan iletir. Aktaran fiil geçmiş zamanda olduğunda (said, told, asked), aktarılan cümlecikteki zaman genellikle bir adım geriye kayar (present→past, past→past perfect, will→would) ve zamirler/zaman ifadeleri yeni konuşan/zaman perspektifine uyacak şekilde değişir (I→he/she, tomorrow→the next day).
structure_patterns: S + asked + if/whether + S + past tense
S + asked + Wh-word + S + V (no auxiliary inversion)
S + told/asked + object + to + V (reported commands/requests)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'Say' bir nesne almaz ('said to me' değil, 'told me'); 'tell' ise mutlaka bir kişi nesnesi ister.

exceptions.rule: If the reporting verb is in the present tense, or if the reported information is a general/timeless truth, no tense backshift is required.
exceptions.example: She says (that) she loves her job. / He said the Earth orbits the Sun.
exceptions.explanation_tr: Aktaran fiil şimdiki zamandaysa veya aktarılan bilgi genel/zamansız bir gerçekse, zaman kaydırma gerekmez.

exceptions.rule: Reported yes/no questions use 'if' or 'whether' and normal statement word order (no auxiliary before the subject), unlike direct questions.
exceptions.example: She asked if I was coming to the party. (NOT: was I coming)
exceptions.explanation_tr: Aktarılan evet/hayır soruları 'if' veya 'whether' kullanır ve doğrudan sorulardan farklı olarak normal ifade kelime sırasını (özneden önce yardımcı fiil yok) alır.

examples.sentence: She said (that) she was tired.
He told me he would call later.
They asked if we had finished the project.
She asked me where I lived.
The doctor told him to rest for a week.
examples.translation: Doktor ona bir hafta dinlenmesini söyledi.

common_mistakes.wrong: She said me that she was tired.
common_mistakes.correct: She told me (that) she was tired.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Say' cannot be directly followed by a personal object; 'tell' must be used when a listener is specified.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Say' fiili doğrudan bir kişi nesnesi alamaz; bir dinleyici belirtildiğinde 'tell' kullanılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: He asked me where did I live.
common_mistakes.correct: He asked me where I lived.
common_mistakes.explanation: Reported questions do not keep the auxiliary-subject inversion of direct questions; normal statement word order is used, and the tense also shifts back.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Aktarılan sorular, doğrudan soruların yardımcı fiil-özne devrik yapısını korumaz; normal ifade kelime sırası kullanılır ve zaman da geriye kayar.

common_mistakes.wrong: She asked if I am coming to the party.
common_mistakes.correct: She asked if I was coming to the party.
common_mistakes.explanation: Since the reporting verb 'asked' is in the past, the reported tense should also shift back one step (am→was), following the standard backshift rule.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Aktaran fiil 'asked' geçmiş zamanda olduğu için, aktarılan zamanın da standart geriye kayma kuralına uyarak bir adım geriye kayması gerekir (am→was).

common_mistakes.wrong: The teacher told that we should study harder.
common_mistakes.correct: The teacher told us (that) we should study harder.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Tell' requires a personal object before the 'that' clause; omitting it (as one might with 'say') is a common cross-verb confusion.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Tell' fiili 'that' cümleciğinden önce bir kişi nesnesi gerektirir; bunu ('say' ile yapıldığı gibi) atlamak yaygın bir fiil karıştırma hatasıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: He said he will come tomorrow.
common_mistakes.correct: He said (that) he would come the next day.
common_mistakes.explanation: With a past reporting verb, 'will' shifts back to 'would', and the time expression 'tomorrow' (relative to the original speech moment) shifts to 'the next day' relative to the new reporting time.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Geçmiş zamanlı bir aktaran fiille birlikte 'will' 'would'a kayar, ve orijinal konuşma anına göre olan 'tomorrow' ifadesi yeni aktarma zamanına göre 'the next day'e kayar.

toefl_style_questions.question: The researcher explained that the results ____ still being analyzed at that time.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Aktaran fiil 'explained' geçmiş zamandadır, bu yüzden aktarılan cümlecikte zaman geriye kayar: are → were.

toefl_style_questions.question: She asked the professor ____ she could submit her assignment a day late.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Bu bir evet/hayır sorusunun aktarımıdır, bu yüzden 'if' (veya 'whether') kullanılır.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests the tense backshift after past reporting verbs, the say/tell object distinction, and word order in reported questions (no auxiliary inversion).

topics.title: used to / would (Past Habits)
topics.explanation: 'Used to' + base verb describes past habits or states that are no longer true, contrasting the past with the present. 'Would' can replace 'used to' for repeated past actions (not states), often in storytelling, but cannot be used for past states like liking, having, or being.
topics.explanation_tr: 'Used to' + yalın fiil, artık geçerli olmayan geçmiş alışkanlık veya durumları anlatır ve geçmişi şimdikiyle karşılaştırır. 'Would', tekrarlanan geçmiş eylemler (durumlar değil) için 'used to'nun yerine geçebilir, genellikle hikaye anlatırken kullanılır; ancak sevme, sahip olma veya olma gibi geçmiş durumlar için kullanılamaz.
structure_patterns: S + used to + V(base) (past habit/state, no longer true)
S + would + V(base) (repeated past action only, not states)
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'Would', 'used to'nun aksine, sahiplik veya duygu bildiren durum fiilleriyle (have, like, be) kullanılamaz.

exceptions.rule: 'Be used to' + noun/gerund means 'to be accustomed to', which is a completely different structure with a different meaning from 'used to + verb'.
exceptions.example: I am used to waking up early. (= I am accustomed to it, an ongoing present habit)
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Be used to' + isim/gerund 'bir şeye alışkın olmak' anlamına gelir; bu, 'used to + fiil'den tamamen farklı bir yapı ve anlamdır.

exceptions.rule: 'Would' cannot describe a past state (be, have, like, know); only 'used to' can be used for these.
exceptions.example: I used to have long hair. (NOT: I would have long hair.)
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Would' geçmiş bir durumu (be, have, like, know) anlatamaz; bunlar için sadece 'used to' kullanılabilir.

examples.sentence: I used to play football every weekend when I was a child.
examples.translation: Çocukken her hafta sonu futbol oynardım.

examples.sentence: She didn't use to like vegetables, but now she loves them.
My grandfather would tell us stories every evening.
examples.translation: Büyükbabam her akşam bize hikayeler anlatırdı.

examples.sentence: There used to be a cinema on this street.
examples.translation: Bu sokakta bir sinema vardı (artık yok).

examples.sentence: Did you use to live in Izmir?

common_mistakes.wrong: I used to have long hair when I was young, so I would have long hair too in college.
common_mistakes.correct: I used to have long hair when I was young, and I still had it in college.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Would' cannot describe the state of having long hair; 'used to' or simple past should be used instead for states.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Would' saç uzunluğu gibi bir durumu anlatamaz; durumlar için 'used to' veya simple past kullanılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: I use to play football when I was a child.
common_mistakes.correct: I used to play football when I was a child.
common_mistakes.explanation: The past habitual form always requires 'used to' (with -d), not the present-tense-looking 'use to'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Geçmiş alışkanlık biçimi her zaman 'used to' (sonunda -d ile) gerektirir, present zaman gibi görünen 'use to' değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: I am use to the cold weather here now.
common_mistakes.correct: I am used to the cold weather here now.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Be used to' (meaning accustomed to) requires 'used', not 'use', even though the pronunciation can make this easy to miss.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Be used to' (alışkın olmak anlamında) 'used' gerektirir, 'use' değil, telaffuzun bunu gözden kaçırmayı kolaylaştırmasına rağmen.

common_mistakes.wrong: Did you used to smoke?
common_mistakes.correct: Did you use to smoke?
common_mistakes.explanation: In questions and negatives with 'did', 'use to' returns to its base form without -d, since 'did' already carries the past tense marking.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Did' ile kurulan soru ve olumsuz cümlelerde 'use to' -d'siz yalın haline döner, çünkü geçmiş zaman işaretini zaten 'did' taşımaktadır.

common_mistakes.wrong: When I was a student, I would live in a small flat.
common_mistakes.correct: When I was a student, I used to live / lived in a small flat.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Live in a flat' as a continuous past state (not a repeated distinct action) is better expressed with 'used to' or simple past, not 'would', which fits repeated distinct actions better.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Bir dairede yaşamak', tekrarlanan ayrı bir eylem değil süregelen bir geçmiş durum olduğu için 'used to' veya simple past ile daha iyi ifade edilir; 'would' tekrarlanan ayrı eylemlere daha uygundur.

toefl_style_questions.question: There ____ a small bookstore on this corner, but it closed down two years ago.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Artık var olmayan bir geçmiş durum anlatıldığı için 'used to' kullanılır; 'would' durum bildiren 'be' ile kullanılmaz.

toefl_style_questions.question: Every summer, my grandmother ____ us to the lake house for a whole month.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Tekrarlanan, ayrı bir eylem (götürmek) anlatıldığı için 'would' burada da doğrudur (used to take de doğru olurdu, ama would özellikle hikaye anlatımında tercih edilir).

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL tests whether 'would' has been incorrectly used for a past state (be, have, like), and checks the 'used to' vs. 'use to' spelling/form depending on whether 'did' is already present.

topics.title: Non-Defining Relative Clauses
topics.explanation: Non-defining relative clauses add extra, non-essential information about a noun that is already fully identified; removing them does not change the core meaning of the sentence. They are always separated by commas, and crucially, 'that' can never be used to introduce a non-defining clause — only who/which/whose/where.
topics.explanation_tr: Tanımlamayan ilgi cümlecikleri, zaten tam olarak tanımlanmış bir isim hakkında ekstra, gerekli olmayan bilgi ekler; çıkarılması cümlenin ana anlamını değiştirmez. Her zaman virgüllerle ayrılır ve önemli olarak, 'that' tanımlamayan bir cümleciği başlatmak için asla kullanılamaz — sadece who/which/whose/where kullanılabilir.
structure_patterns: S + V + noun, which/who + extra info (end of sentence)
..., which + comment on the whole previous clause
topics.signal_words_note_tr: Virgül varlığı, cümleciğin tanımlayan mı tanımlamayan mı olduğunu belirleyen en açık işarettir.

exceptions.rule: 'That' is never used in a non-defining relative clause, even though it is fine in a defining one.
exceptions.example: My father, who is 70 years old, still works every day. (NOT: My father, that is 70...)
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'That', tanımlayan cümlecikte uygun olsa da tanımlamayan cümlecikte asla kullanılmaz.

exceptions.rule: 'Which' can refer back to an entire previous clause/idea, not just a single noun, functioning as a comment on the whole situation.
exceptions.example: He forgot her birthday, which upset her a lot.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Which' sadece tek bir isme değil, önceki bütün bir cümleye/fikre atıfta bulunarak durumun tamamı hakkında bir yorum işlevi görebilir.

examples.sentence: My sister, who lives in Berlin, is visiting us next month.
examples.translation: Berlin'de yaşayan kız kardeşim gelecek ay bizi ziyaret ediyor.

examples.sentence: The Eiffel Tower, which was completed in 1889, attracts millions of visitors.
examples.translation: 1889'da tamamlanan Eyfel Kulesi milyonlarca ziyaretçi çekiyor.

examples.sentence: Mr. Johnson, whose son studies with me, is a well-known lawyer.
examples.translation: Oğlu benimle okuyan Bay Johnson tanınmış bir avukat.

examples.sentence: We visited Kyoto, where my grandparents were born.
examples.translation: Büyükanne ve büyükbabamın doğduğu Kyoto'yu ziyaret ettik.

examples.sentence: The meeting was postponed, which annoyed everyone.
examples.translation: Toplantı ertelendi, bu da herkesi kızdırdı.

common_mistakes.wrong: My father that is 70 years old still works every day.
common_mistakes.correct: My father, who is 70 years old, still works every day.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'That' cannot be used in a non-defining relative clause; 'who' must be used, and the clause must be set off with commas.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'That' tanımlamayan bir ilgi cümleciğinde kullanılamaz; 'who' kullanılmalı ve cümlecik virgüllerle ayrılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: The Eiffel Tower which was completed in 1889 attracts millions of visitors.
common_mistakes.correct: The Eiffel Tower, which was completed in 1889, attracts millions of visitors.
common_mistakes.explanation: Since the Eiffel Tower is already fully identified by its name, the extra information about its completion date must be set off by commas as a non-defining clause.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Eyfel Kulesi zaten adıyla tam olarak tanımlandığı için, tamamlanma tarihiyle ilgili ek bilgi tanımlamayan cümlecik olarak virgüllerle ayrılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: My sister, she lives in Berlin, is visiting us next month.
common_mistakes.correct: My sister, who lives in Berlin, is visiting us next month.
common_mistakes.explanation: A relative pronoun (who) must replace the subject pronoun (she); keeping both creates a double subject inside the clause.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Bir ilgi zamiri (who) özne zamirinin (she) yerini almalıdır; ikisini birlikte tutmak cümlecik içinde çift özne oluşturur.

common_mistakes.wrong: He forgot her birthday, that upset her a lot.
common_mistakes.correct: He forgot her birthday, which upset her a lot.
common_mistakes.explanation: When referring back to an entire preceding idea (not a single noun), 'which' is required, and 'that' is never used after a comma in this function.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Tek bir isme değil önceki bütün bir fikre atıfta bulunulurken 'which' gereklidir; bu işlevde virgülden sonra 'that' asla kullanılmaz.

common_mistakes.wrong: Mr. Johnson who his son studies with me is a well-known lawyer.
common_mistakes.correct: Mr. Johnson, whose son studies with me, is a well-known lawyer.
common_mistakes.explanation: To show possession (his son), the possessive relative pronoun 'whose' must be used, not 'who' combined with a separate possessive adjective, and commas are required since this is extra information.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Sahiplik ilişkisini (his son) göstermek için iyelik ilgi zamiri 'whose' kullanılmalıdır, 'who' ile ayrı bir iyelik sıfatının birleşimi değil; bu ek bilgi olduğu için virgüller de gereklidir.

toefl_style_questions.question: Marie Curie, ____ discovered two new elements, remains one of the most celebrated scientists in history.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Bu bir insana (Marie Curie) atıfta bulunan tanımlamayan bir cümleciktir; 'that' burada kullanılamaz, 'who' doğru seçimdir.

toefl_style_questions.question: The company announced record profits, ____ came as a surprise to most analysts.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Which' burada tek bir isme değil, kâr açıklamasının tamamına atıfta bulunur; virgülden sonra 'that' kullanılamaz.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL specifically tests whether 'that' has been wrongly used after a comma (which is always incorrect), and checks whether a double subject remains inside a relative clause.

topics.title: Quantifiers: few vs. a few, little vs. a little, most/majority
topics.title_tr: İleri Miktar Belirteçleri: few vs. a few, little vs. a little, most/majority
topics.explanation: 'A few' and 'a little' have a positive meaning (some, a small but sufficient amount), while 'few' and 'little' (without 'a') have a negative meaning (almost none, not enough) — the presence or absence of the article completely reverses the emotional tone, even though the words look almost identical. 'Most of' and 'the majority of' both express a large proportion but require different grammatical structures depending on definiteness.
topics.explanation_tr: 'A few' ve 'a little' olumlu bir anlam taşır (biraz, az ama yeterli bir miktar); 'few' ve 'little' ('a' olmadan) ise olumsuz bir anlam taşır (neredeyse hiç, yetersiz) — artikelin varlığı veya yokluğu, kelimeler neredeyse aynı görünse de duygusal tonu tamamen tersine çevirir. 'Most of' ve 'the majority of' ikisi de büyük bir oranı ifade eder ancak belirlilik durumuna göre farklı dilbilgisel yapılar gerektirir.
structure_patterns: a few/a little + noun (positive: some, enough)
most + noun (general) vs. most of + the/my/these + noun (specific)
the majority of + plural noun + plural verb
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'A' harfinin varlığı anlamı olumludan olumsuza çevirir; bu, TOEFL'da sık test edilen ince bir ayrımdır.

exceptions.rule: 'Most' is used generally without 'of' before a plural noun with no specific determiner, but 'most of' is required before a specific/definite noun phrase (the, my, these, us).
exceptions.example: Most students like holidays. / Most of the students in my class like holidays.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Most', belirli bir belirteç olmadan genel bir çoğul isimden önce 'of' almadan kullanılır; ama belirli/tanımlı bir isim öbeğinden (the, my, these, us) önce 'most of' gerekir.

exceptions.rule: 'The majority of' behaves grammatically like 'most of' and takes a plural verb when followed by a plural noun.
exceptions.example: The majority of voters support the new policy.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'The majority of' dilbilgisel olarak 'most of' gibi davranır ve çoğul bir isimden sonra çoğul fiil alır.

examples.sentence: We have a few options left, so don't worry.
examples.translation: Elimizde birkaç seçenek kaldı, merak etme.

examples.sentence: There is little hope of finding survivors.
examples.translation: Hayatta kalan bulma umudu çok az.

examples.sentence: Most of the students in my class passed the exam.
The majority of the population lives in urban areas.
She has a little experience in marketing, which should help.
examples.translation: Pazarlamada biraz deneyimi var, bu yardımcı olacaktır.

common_mistakes.wrong: Don't worry, we have few options left.
common_mistakes.correct: Don't worry, we have a few options left.
common_mistakes.explanation: Without 'a', 'few' has a negative meaning (almost no options), which contradicts the reassuring tone of 'don't worry'; the positive 'a few' is needed.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'A' olmadan 'few' olumsuz bir anlam taşır (neredeyse hiç seçenek yok), bu da 'don't worry'nin güven verici tonuyla çelişir; olumlu 'a few' gereklidir.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have a little time, so I can't help you today.
common_mistakes.correct: I have little time, so I can't help you today.
common_mistakes.explanation: Since the sentence expresses inability due to insufficient time, the negative 'little' (without 'a') is required, not the positive 'a little'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: Cümle yetersiz zaman nedeniyle yetersizlik ifade ettiği için, olumlu 'a little' değil olumsuz 'little' (a'sız) gereklidir.

common_mistakes.wrong: Most of students like holidays.
common_mistakes.correct: Most students like holidays. / Most of the students like holidays.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Most of' requires a definite/specific noun phrase (the, my, these); a bare plural noun with no determiner should follow plain 'most' instead.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Most of' belirli/tanımlı bir isim öbeği (the, my, these) gerektirir; belirteci olmayan yalın bir çoğul isim, düz 'most' ile kullanılmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: The majority of the workers has already left the factory.
common_mistakes.correct: The majority of the workers have already left the factory.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'The majority of' behaves grammatically like 'most of': the verb agrees with the plural noun that follows it (workers), so 'have' is required, not the singular 'has'.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'The majority of', dilbilgisel olarak 'most of' gibi davranır: fiil, kendisinden sonra gelen çoğul isimle (workers) uyumlanır, bu yüzden 'have' gerekir, tekil 'has' değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: Few of my friends is coming to the party.
common_mistakes.correct: Few of my friends are coming to the party.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Few of + plural noun' takes a plural verb (are), not a singular verb (is).
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Few of + çoğul isim' çoğul fiil alır (are), tekil fiil değil (is).

toefl_style_questions.question: Fortunately, ____ old friends were able to attend the reunion despite the short notice.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Fortunately' olumlu bir ton taşır: kısa bildirime rağmen birilerinin katılabilmiş olması sevindiricidir, bu yüzden olumlu anlamlı 'a few' gereklidir. 'Few' (olumsuz, 'neredeyse hiç kimse gelemedi') buradaki sevindirici tonla çelişirdi.

toefl_style_questions.question: Unfortunately, ____ evidence was available to support the claim, so the case was dismissed.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: 'Unfortunately' ve 'dismissed' yetersizliği ima eder, bu yüzden olumsuz anlamlı 'little' (a'sız) gereklidir.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL frequently tests the article-driven meaning flip between few/a few and little/a little, using surrounding context words (fortunately/unfortunately, so/but) as clues.

topics.title: Linking Words of Contrast and Concession
topics.explanation: Words like 'although', 'even though', 'despite', 'in spite of', and 'however' all express contrast or concession, but they differ grammatically: 'although/even though' are followed by a full clause (subject + verb), while 'despite/in spite of' are followed by a noun phrase or gerund, never a full clause with a conjugated verb. 'However' connects two separate sentences and is usually followed by a comma, not a clause directly.
topics.explanation_tr: 'Although', 'even though', 'despite', 'in spite of' ve 'however' gibi kelimeler hepsi karşıtlık veya uzlaşma ifade eder, ancak dilbilgisel olarak farklıdır: 'although/even though'dan sonra tam bir cümlecik (özne + fiil) gelir; 'despite/in spite of'tan sonra ise bir isim öbeği veya gerund gelir, asla çekimli fiilli tam bir cümlecik gelmez. 'However' iki ayrı cümleyi bağlar ve genellikle sonrasında virgül gelir, doğrudan bir cümlecik değil.
structure_patterns: Although/Even though + S + V, S + V
Despite/In spite of + noun phrase/gerund, S + V
topics.signal_words_note_tr: 'Despite' ve 'in spite of'tan sonra asla özne+fiil gelmez; sadece isim öbeği veya -ing formu gelir.

exceptions.rule: To follow 'despite/in spite of' with a full clause-like idea, the structure 'despite/in spite of the fact that + clause' must be used instead.
exceptions.example: Despite the fact that it was raining, we went for a walk.
exceptions.explanation_tr: 'Despite/in spite of'ı tam bir cümlecik benzeri fikirle takip etmek için 'despite/in spite of the fact that + cümlecik' yapısı kullanılmalıdır.

exceptions.rule: 'However' at the start of a sentence is usually followed by a comma, distinguishing it from 'but', which connects within a single sentence without starting a new one (in standard punctuation).
exceptions.example: The plan was risky. However, it succeeded.
exceptions.explanation_tr: Cümle başındaki 'however'dan sonra genellikle virgül gelir; bu, yeni bir cümle başlatmadan aynı cümle içinde bağlantı kuran 'but'tan onu ayırır (standart noktalamada).

examples.sentence: Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
Despite the heavy traffic, she arrived on time.
The team lost the match. However, they played very well.
examples.translation: Takım maçı kaybetti. Ancak, çok iyi oynadılar.

examples.sentence: In spite of his busy schedule, he always finds time to read.
examples.translation: Yoğun programına rağmen her zaman okumaya vakit buluyor.

examples.sentence: She is very talented, yet she remains humble.

common_mistakes.wrong: Despite it was raining, we went for a walk.
common_mistakes.correct: Despite the rain, we went for a walk. / Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Despite' cannot be followed directly by a clause with a conjugated verb (it was); it must be followed by a noun phrase, or the sentence should use 'although' instead.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Despite'ten sonra çekimli fiilli bir cümlecik (it was) doğrudan gelemez; bir isim öbeği gelmelidir, ya da cümle 'although' kullanmalıdır.

common_mistakes.wrong: Although the heavy traffic, she arrived on time.
common_mistakes.correct: Despite the heavy traffic, she arrived on time. / Although there was heavy traffic, she arrived on time.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Although' must be followed by a full clause (subject + verb), not a bare noun phrase; 'despite' is the correct choice before a noun phrase alone.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Although'dan sonra tam bir cümlecik (özne + fiil) gelmelidir, yalın bir isim öbeği değil; sadece isim öbeğinden önce doğru seçim 'despite'tir.

common_mistakes.wrong: The team lost the match, however they played very well.
common_mistakes.correct: The team lost the match. However, they played very well. / The team lost the match; however, they played very well.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'However' cannot join two clauses with just a comma the way 'but' can; it needs a full stop or semicolon before it, followed by its own comma.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'However', 'but'ın yaptığı gibi iki cümleciği sadece virgülle birleştiremez; öncesinde nokta veya noktalı virgül, kendi ardından da virgül gerekir.

common_mistakes.wrong: In spite of he is busy, he always finds time to read.
common_mistakes.correct: In spite of being busy, he always finds time to read. / Even though he is busy, he always finds time to read.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'In spite of' must be followed by a noun phrase or gerund (being busy), not a subject + conjugated verb clause (he is busy).
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'In spite of'tan sonra bir isim öbeği veya gerund (being busy) gelmelidir, özne + çekimli fiil cümleciği (he is busy) değil.

common_mistakes.wrong: Even though of the rain, we went outside.
common_mistakes.correct: Even though it rained, we went outside. / Despite the rain, we went outside.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Even though' behaves like 'although' and must be followed by a full clause, never by 'of + noun', which mixes it incorrectly with 'despite'/'in spite of' patterns.
common_mistakes.explanation_tr: 'Even though', 'although' gibi davranır ve her zaman tam bir cümlecikle takip edilmelidir; asla 'of + isim' ile kullanılmaz, bu 'despite'/'in spite of' kalıplarıyla yanlış bir karışımdır.

toefl_style_questions.question: ____ the company's strong financial performance, its stock price fell sharply last week.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Sonrasında bir isim öbeği ('the company's strong financial performance') geldiği için 'despite' kullanılır, 'although/even though' değil.

toefl_style_questions.question: The experiment failed to produce the expected results; ____, the researchers gained valuable insight into the process.
toefl_style_questions.explanation_tr: Noktalı virgülden sonra iki bağımsız cümleciği bağlamak için 'however' kullanılır, ardından virgül gelir.

topics.toefl_tip: TOEFL heavily tests whether 'despite/in spite of' is wrongly followed by a full clause, and whether 'although/even though' is wrongly followed by a bare noun phrase, plus the punctuation pattern around 'however'.

topics.title: Third and Mixed Conditionals
topics.explanation: The third conditional (If + past perfect, ... would have + past participle) expresses an unreal past situation and its imagined past result — used for regret or speculation about something that did not happen. Mixed conditionals combine a past condition with a present result (or vice versa), used when the time of the condition and the time of the result are different.
